https://novastan.org/de/politik-und-wirt.body: 7. Juni 2026 La rédaction Übersetzt von: Michèle Häfliger Original (4. Juni 2026) Schlagwörter Arbeitsmigranten Crocus City Hall Gefängnis Genfer Konventionen Islamischer Staat Khorasan Krieg Kriegsgefangene Militär Russland Sowjetunion Staatsbürgerschaft Ukraine Kriegsgefangene marschieren in ihre Zellen, 15. April 2026. Foto: Driss Rejichi Bürger aus Zentralasien stellen den größten Anteil ausländischer Kämpfer in der russischen Armee. Novastan hat mehrere von ihnen, die von ukrainischen Streitkräften gefangen genommen wurden, aufgesucht. Ihre Berichte verdeutlichen, wie Migranten aus Zentralasien für Moskau zu einer Quelle besonders anfälliger Rekruten geworden sind. Im Hof einer Militärstrafanstalt in der Region Lviv im Westen der Ukraine schreiten Dutzende von Gefangenen schweigend zum Speisesaal. An den Wänden um sie herum hängen Porträts von Daniel von Galizien , Stepan Bandera und anderen ukrainischen Nationalisten. Im größten Kriegsgefangenenlager des Landes sind alle Beschriftungen und Befehle auf Ukrainisch verfasst. „Bei uns läuft alles gut, sie sind ruhig, es gibt keine Schlägereien“ , erzählt ein Wachmann. Vor seinen Augen betreten die Gefangenen die Kantine zum Mittagessen. Ihre Gesichter sind verschlossen. Einige Häftlinge haben bereits vier Jahre im Lager verbracht. Vor allem weist ein Großteil von ihnen deutlich asiatische Gesichtszüge auf. Bei einigen handelt es sich um Russen aus sibirischen Republiken wie Burjatien und Jakutien, wo die Einberufungsquoten besonders hoch sind. Kantine des Kriegsgefangenen-Camps am 15. April 2026. Foto: Driss Rejichi Viele andere sind Soldaten aus den fünf ehemaligen Sowjetrepubliken Zentralasiens. „Die meisten Ausländer, die ich in der russischen Armee gesehen habe, kamen von dort“ , erklärt Chuschbacht Perusalijew. Im Frühjahr 2024 unterzeichnete der 47-jährige Tadschike einen Vertrag, um in der russischen Armee zu dienen. „Man sagte mir: ‚Du wirst nicht an der Front sein, nichts dergleichen, du wirst einfach in einem Lager arbeiten‘ ... Also habe ich zugestimmt“ , erinnert sich der Mann mit rasiertem Kopf und Bart. Eine Lüge: Wenige Wochen später wurde der Tadschike von ukrainischen Streitkräften gefangen genommen, nachdem er bei einem Frontalangriff im Gebiet Donezk verwundet worden war. Weit vor den 1.400 Männern aus afrikanischen Ländern oder den 200 indischen Staatsbürgern, die seit Kriegsbeginn von der russischen Armee rekrutiert wurden, sollen laut den im April 2026 von der ukrainischen Koordinierungsstelle für Kriegsgefangene veröffentlichten Daten bereits mehr als 12.000 Soldaten aus Zentralasien an der „militärischen Sonderoperation“ in der Ukraine teilgenommen haben. Mehr als die Hälfte der ausländischen Kämpfer, die für Russland kämpfen, stammen somit aus dieser Region. Angesichts von Razzien und Ausweisungen: das Versprechen eines Passes Alle zentralasiatischen Kriegsgefangenen, mit denen Novastan gesprochen hat, befanden sich im Gefängnis von Mykolajiv und waren bereits vor 2022 in Russland. „Die Rekrutierungsbemühungen, die sich an Ausländer richten, konzentrieren sich auf Arbeitsmigranten und Häftlinge, die eine Freiheitsstrafe verbüßen“ , betont ein Offizier der ukrainischen Koordinierungsstelle für Kriegsgefangene. Iljas, ein kirgistanischer Staatsbürger und Getränkehändler, der seit 2007 in Moskau lebt, unterzeichnete seinen Vertrag im April 2025. „Mir wurde bei der Rekrutierung nicht direkt die Staatsbürgerschaft versprochen, aber ich wusste, dass ich später die Möglichkeit haben würde, sie zu erhalten“ , erklärt der Vierzigjährige. Unterstützt Novastan – das europäische Zentralasien-Magazin Als vereinsgetragene, unabhängige Plattform lebt Novastan vom Enthusiasmus seiner ehrenamtlichen Mitarbeiter:innen – und von eurer Unterstützung! Novastan unterstützen Im Januar 2024 unterzeichnete Wladimir Putin ein Dekret, das es ermöglichte, bestimmten Ausländern, die in der Armee gedient hatten, insbesondere während der „militärischen Sonderoperation“, die Staatsbürgerschaft zu gewähren. Die Zahl der Ausländer, die davon profitiert haben, ist nach wie vor unbekannt. In der Ukraine berichten die zentralasiatischen Gefangenen übereinstimmend, dass sie nach einer kurzen Ausbildung an die Front geschickt wurden, was zu hohen Verlusten führte. „Wir rückten auf ein Dorf vor, und schon auf dem Weg dorthin tauchten Drohnen auf und begannen, uns anzugreifen“ , erinnert sich Iljas, der knapp entkommen konnte und anschließend gefangen genommen wurde. Chuschbacht wurde seinerseits bei einem Artillerieangriff verwundet, als er auf die ukrainischen Linien vorrückte: „Die Hälfte der Gruppe fiel sofort, alle 200 [russischer Militärcode für Tote, Anm. d. Red.]“ . Der Familienvater, dessen Frau und Kinder noch immer in Rjasan , 200 Kilometer südöstlich von Moskau, leben, beschreibt, wie „unmittelbar nach dem Anschlag auf die Crocus City Hall“ im März 2024 ein Klima der Angst herrschte. Der von tadschikistanischen Staatsbürgern verübte und vom Islamischen Staat Khorasan beanspruchte Terroranschlag forderte mehr als 149 Todesopfer und führte zu einer Verschärfung der Lebensbedingungen für Migrierte aus Zentralasien in Russland. Laut Chuschbacht kam es häufig zu „Razzien gegen Tadschiken“ , bei denen den Migranten „sofort die Abschiebung mit Einreiseverbot“ auferlegt wurde. Lest auch auf Novastan: Werden die Angeklagten im Fall Crocus City Hall ausgeliefert? Aus Angst verzichtete der Mann darauf, seinen abgelaufenen Pass verlängern zu lassen, aus Furcht, auf dem Weg zur Botschaft in Moskau festgenommen zu werden. „Schließlich kontrollierten Spezialeinheiten der Polizei die Baustelle, auf der ich arbeitete“ , erklärt der Migrant, dem daraufhin die Staatsbürgerschaft versprochen wurde, wenn er sich der Armee anschließe. „Es stimmt, dass Tadschiken nach dem Anschlag auf die Crocus City Hall stärker ins Visier genommen wurden als andere Gruppen aus Zentralasien“ , betont Caress Schenk, Professorin für Politikwissenschaft an der Nazarbaev-Universität in Astana. Nach Angaben der ukrainischen Koordinierungsstelle für Kriegsgefangene sind Tadschiken mit mehr als 3.400 Rekruten die zweitgrößte Nationalität in der russischen Armee, hinter etwa 4.800 Usbeken und 2.400 Kasachen. Lest auch auf Novastan: Kopftuch und Bart – Migrant:innen aus Zentralasien über Islamophobie in Russland Schenk weist jedoch darauf hin, dass in Russland „die Maßnahmen zur Migrationskontrolle, Razzien und der Druck, zum Militär zu gehen, stark von der aktuellen Lage abhängen“ . Seit Kriegsbeginn konnten je nach Kontext auch andere Bevölkerungsgruppen ins Visier geraten. „Manchmal gerät jede Person mit asiatischen Gesichtszügen unter Verdacht“ , bemerkt die Forscherin. Seit November 2025 müssen bestimmte in Russland lebende Ausländer einen Vertrag über den Eintritt in die Armee vorlegen, wenn sie die russische Staatsbürgerschaft oder eine Aufenthaltsgenehmigung erhalten wollen. Zu Beginn des Jahrzehnts machten Zentralasiaten jedoch mehr als 40 Prozent der in Russland lebenden Migranten aus und sind daher am stärksten von diesen neuen Maßnahmen betroffen. Zwar erklären alle von Novastan befragten Gefangenen, ihren Vertrag freiwillig unterzeichnet zu haben, um einen russischen Pass zu erhalten, doch betont Schenk auch, dass der zunehmende administrative Druck „eher darauf abzielt, die Handlungs- und Entscheidungsfähigkeit der Migranten einzuschränken, als ihnen echte Wahlmöglichkeiten zu bieten.“ Ideologisch gefährdete Migranten Neben der prekären administrativen Lage stützt sich die russische Armee bei ihren Mobilisierungsbemühungen auch auf mögliche ideologische Affinitäten der zentralasiatischen Migranten. „Ich wollte in Russland leben. Um die Staatsbürgerschaft zu erlangen, auf die ich meiner Meinung nach Anspruch hatte, musste ich also dem Vaterland dienen“ , erklärt der 38-jährige Jasur Islamov in einem gleichgültigen Ton. Nach anderthalb Jahren in der Armee wird ihm im März 2025 endlich der Pass versprochen, sofern er an der Front bleibt

https://novastan.org/fr/kazakhstan/mongo.body: 10 septembre 2026 Rédigé par : Mathieu Lemoine Traduit par : Mathieu Lemoine Tags Asie centrale Chine Mongolie Russie Bolor Lkhaajav. Soutenez Novastan, le média associatif d’Asie centrale En vous abonnant à Novastan, vous soutenez le seul média européen spécialisé sur l’Asie centrale. Nous sommes indépendants et pour le rester, nous avons besoin de votre aide ! A partir de 3 € / mois Toute l’actualité d’Asie centrale Abonnez-vous La position de la Mongolie entre la Russie et la Chine est souvent présentée comme une contrainte géopolitique. La chercheuse et autrice Bolor Lkhaajav estime au contraire qu’Oulan-Bator cherche à combiner des relations solides avec ses deux voisins et une politique du « troisième voisin » de plus en plus ambitieuse, qui couvre les minerais critiques, l’énergie, les technologies, la diplomatie et la sécurité. Bolor Lkhaajav est spécialiste de l’Asie de l’Est et du Nord-Est et a publié plus de 200 articles et analyses dans plusieurs langues. Elle écrit régulièrement sur l’histoire diplomatique, les politiques étrangères et de sécurité, la géopolitique, l’économie, la politique et la société. Elle travaille actuellement sur la grande stratégie de politique étrangère de la Mongolie et a été admise dans un programme de doctorat qui débutera à l’automne 2027. Dans cet entretien avec Novastan, elle revient sur la manière dont la Mongolie s’adapte aux conséquences géopolitiques de l’invasion à grande échelle de l’Ukraine par la Russie, sur l’importance croissante de la Corée du Sud et des autres « troisièmes voisins », sur le potentiel du pays en matière de minerais critiques, sur les pressions environnementales et sur la position singulière de la Mongolie dans une Asie du Nord-Est en pleine mutation. Novastan : Vous travaillez actuellement sur la grande stratégie de politique étrangère de la Mongolie. Comment décririez-vous l’approche stratégique du pays aujourd’hui, et comment a-t-elle évolué dans le nouvel environnement géopolitique depuis l’invasion à grande échelle de l’Ukraine par la Russie ? Bolor Lkhaajav : En 2011, le Parlement mongol a adopté le Concept de politique étrangère du pays, un document juridique définissant la stratégie de politique étrangère d’Oulan-Bator afin de répondre aux exigences contemporaines tout en maintenant un équilibre entre ses deux voisins, la Russie et la Chine. L’un des éléments importants de ce concept a été l’introduction formelle de la doctrine du « troisième voisin ». L’idée d’un « troisième voisin » existait depuis longtemps dans l’histoire mongole et dans les milieux diplomatiques, mais elle n’avait jamais été définie ni appliquée de manière aussi explicite et transparente. Depuis 2011, cette politique est devenue l’un des piliers de la grande stratégie de politique étrangère de la Mongolie. Elle vise précisément à renforcer les liens diplomatiques, politiques, économiques et culturels de la Mongolie avec des pays autres que la Russie et la Chine, tout en consolidant dans le même temps les relations bilatérales et trilatérales avec Moscou et Pékin. Depuis l’invasion de l’Ukraine par la Russie, la Mongolie subit les conséquences de la priorité donnée par Moscou à son approvisionnement énergétique intérieur. Compte tenu de la forte dépendance de la Mongolie aux carburants russes, les pénuries intermittentes sont devenues récurrentes au cours des six derniers mois. Cela montre également pourquoi il est essentiel pour la Mongolie d’investir dans les énergies renouvelables et de travailler avec ses partenaires du troisième voisin afin de renforcer le secteur énergétique du pays. La grande stratégie mongole vise à positionner Oulan-Bator comme un acteur stable et démocratique sur la scène internationale. Elle ne dépend pas des politiques étrangères de ses voisins, ni de celles d’un autre pays, ni de leur engagement sur la scène mondiale. La Mongolie peut réagir différemment aux défis extérieurs, mais ceux-ci ne modifieront pas fondamentalement sa grande stratégie de politique étrangère. La doctrine mongole du « troisième voisin » fournit un cadre beaucoup plus large, qui prévoit des mécanismes de coopération dans différents secteurs et à différentes étapes du développement. Elle ne se limite pas au secteur minier. https://uznews.uz/en/news/103522.body: Home Popular News feed Reels Экономика Интервью Общество Спорт Назначения Происшествия Культура president.uz 17 сентября в Намангане Шавкат Мирзиёев выступил на III международном форуме «От бедности к процветанию». Глава государства отметил, что на фоне геополитической, экономической и социальной нестабильности в мире, а также из-за последствий изменения климата темпы глобального экономического роста замедлились, что в свою очередь привело к увеличению числа малоимущих. В столь сложный период в Узбекистане борьба с бедностью возведена в ранг государственной политики. Все усилия нацелены на то, чтобы каждый человек мог в полной мере раскрыть свой потенциал. В обновлённой Конституции закреплено, что размеры пенсий, пособий и социальной помощи не могут быть ниже минимальных потребительских расходов. Благодаря последовательным реформам 7,5 млн человек выведены из состояния бедности, а в 2024 году её уровень снижен до 8,9%. До конца года поставлена задача уменьшить показатель до 6%. Существенную роль сыграл рост экономики в 2 раза. Ожидается, что доход на душу населения по итогам года достигнет $3500. На основе апробации новых инициатив и изучения передовой мировой практики сформирована модель Нового Узбекистана по сокращению бедности. Введены адресные социальные реестры, в период пандемии на бесплатные лекарства и социальные выплаты направлено в общей сложности $8 млрд. Это позволило не допустить попадания 5,2 млн граждан в «ловушку бедности» и предотвратить экономическую рецессию. Также внедрена система работы в разрезе махалли – на самом низовом уровне. С каждой семьёй ведётся индивидуальная работа, выделяются необходимые ресурсы для наращивания доходов. Ежегодно на благоустройство махаллей, улучшение жизни людей и развитие инфраструктуры предпринимательства направляется $2,5–3 млрд. Для повышения доходов сельских жителей на 235 тысячах гектаров сокращены площади под хлопком и зерновыми, а гражданам выделены участки по 30–50 соток. Это стало важным шагом к росту доходов 800 тысяч человек. «Благодаря столь масштабным усилиям Узбекистан стремится досрочно выполнить взятое обязательство — сократить бедность вдвое к 2030 году. Более того, сегодня мы готовы определить ещё более высокую планку: к 2030 году по международным критериям в Узбекистане есть все возможности полностью искоренить абсолютную бедность, и мы обязательно этого добьёмся, – подчеркнул президент. 3388 Share Telegram Facebook

We’re independent and we need your help to stay that way! Support Novastan From horse archers and traditional dress to carefully staged portraits, Mongolian photographer Ganzorig Miimaa draws on the country’s nomadic heritage to create a contemporary visual language. The 500px Photographer of the Year 2025 speaks to Novastan about looking at Mongolia differently, the new generation transforming tradition, and why a childhood question about Mortal Kombat still shapes his work. Mongolian photographer Ganzorig Miimaa spent the early years of his career looking outward. Like many young photographers, he drew inspiration from images circulating internationally. He wanted the Mongolian people he photographed to appear “international, modern, fashionable, or classical”. Gradually, however, he began to realise that some of his strongest subjects were already around him: Mongolia’s nomadic life, history, people and cultural heritage. Read more on Novastan : “Mongolia cannot be understood through one lens”: Dr. Mendee Jargalsaikhan on democracy, China and Central Asia The shift has come to define his photography. Based in Ulaanbaatar and with more than fifteen years of professional experience, Ganzorig works across portrait, documentary, commercial and staged photography. In 2025, he was named Photographer of the Year at the 500px Global Photography Awards . His portrait Queen , inspired by the elaborate hairstyles worn by Mongolian women historically, also received the competition’s Judges’ Choice award in the Portrait category. In 2026, his Ornamented Identity took second place in the professional division of the reFocus Black & White Photo Contest . Yet Ganzorig’s work is not primarily an exercise in documenting disappearing traditions. His photographs often reconstruct them. Historical clothing, horses, archery, hunting practices and other elements of Mongolia’s visual heritage are placed within carefully controlled compositions, where lighting, colour, pose and environment become as important as the subjects themselves. It is an approach that reflects something he sees happening more widely in contemporary Mongolia. A younger generation of artists, he argues, is increasingly treating cultural heritage not simply as something inherited and protected, but as material from which something new can be created. Novastan English Editor-in-Chief Mathieu Lemoine spoke with Ganzorig Miimaa about photography, cultural identity and what it means to make Mongolia visible to the outside world. Novastan: Your recent work often explores Mongolian identity, heritage and the relationship between tradition and contemporary life. What does “Mongolian identity” mean to you visually, and how has your understanding of it changed through photography? Ganzorig Miimaa: It is difficult for me to define exactly what makes Mongolian identity unique, because I have not studied other cultures deeply enough to make that kind of comparison. But I do believe that Mongolia’s vast history, and the nomadic way of life that continues to this day, are something very special. When I first started photography, I tried to make images similar to the ones I saw on international photography platforms. I wanted to make Mongolian people look more international, modern, fashionable, or classical. Read more on Novastan : Central Asia through the lens of... Behzod Boltayev Over time, I began to realise that rather than following what everyone else was doing, it was more important to find and bring out things around me that others had not yet noticed or seen. Mongolia’s history, nomadic life, people and cultural heritage gradually became some of the closest and strongest sources of visual inspiration for me. When you photograph subjects that outsiders strongly associate with Mongolia – horses, eagle hunters, traditional dress, the steppe – what do you look for that makes the image feel personal rather than expected? Because my background is in advertising photography, I pay a great deal of attention not only to the idea or content of an image, but also to its visual and aesthetic qualities. I would probably divide this kind of work into two categories. The first consists of photographs I make while researching a subject, meeting people and travelling – images that come from real situations and events as they happen. Read more on Novastan : Central Asia through the lens of... Kamila Rustambekova The second consists of fully staged photographs, where I already have an image in my mind of how I want something to look. With these photographs, I work much more deliberately with lighting, colour, composition, environment and the positioning of the subject, and I try to introduce a degree of artistic interpretation and abstraction. So when I photograph subjects that are already strongly associated with Mongolia, it is less about trying to find a completely different subject and more about finding a way to show it through my own visual language. What usually comes first for you when making a photograph: a face, a gesture, a landscape, a colour, a story or an idea? Ideas can come from many different things, and very often they eventually intersect. For example, I might see someone and think, “I would really like to photograph this person.” Then, sometime later, I might witness an event and suddenly think, “This could be an interesting way to photograph that person.” Later still, I might see a location or an object and think, “This would be the right place for it.” Things that originally had no connection to one another gradually come together in a single photograph. But there is no fixed order. Sometimes the location comes first, sometimes the person, sometimes a story, or simply an image that appears in my mind. For me, a photograph often develops through connections between things I have noticed at completely different times. In projects such as Ornamented Identity , you work with carefully constructed portraits and visual symbolism. How do you decide when to stage an image and when to work more observationally or documentarily? Honestly, there is not a particularly deep philosophy behind that decision. If it were possible, I would probably stage almost all of my photographs and control every element of the image myself. But in reality, sometimes the most practical option is to photograph something while it is actually happening. Recreating an event later might require coordinating the schedules of many people, as well as arranging costumes, horses, locations, transportation and many other things. The cost of the shoot can also increase very quickly. So some of my observational or documentary photographs are not necessarily the result of a deliberate artistic principle. Sometimes they are simply about making the best use of the opportunity that exists at that moment. When circumstances allow, I prefer to plan an image carefully and construct it. Where in Mongolia do you personally find the strongest artistic inspiration? Are there particular regions, landscapes or communities that continue to draw you back? One of the places that gives me the most inspiration and material for research is the Nomads Festival . Cultural heritage practitioners from Mongolia’s 21 provinces gather in one place and present their ways of life, customs, crafts, clothing, traditional knowledge and skills out on the open steppe. For me, it is an opportunity to encounter an enormous amount of information about the cultures of different regions of Mongolia in a very short period of time. For citation and references to the material, please indicate: Aigerim Kussaiynkyzy, Reintegration of women after release: Barriers, Success Factors and Measures to Strengthen Probation in the Republic of Kazakhstan (white paper) 2026, CABAR.asia. The publication notes that international guidelines on women’s health in prison and upon release emphasize the increased prevalence of mental health issues among female prisoners and the need for continuous care for this population. In 2025, Kazakhstan held an amnesty to mark the 30th anniversary of the Constitution. Initially, it was estimated that it would benefit up to 15,000 people, with a combination of release and sentence reduction. By January 2026, it was reported that more than 2,000 people had been released under the amnesty, and more than 11,000 had received sentence reductions. The findings of the white paper are based on a study conducted in the Karaganda region of Kazakhstan. The study focused on the law enforcement practices of entities involved in the resocialization of women after imprisonment. Based on field research (surveys in penal institutions, expert interviews, and official responses from government agencies), practical, measurable, and feasible measures are proposed to improve the effectiveness of post-penitentiary support and strengthen the social component of probation. Thus, the White Paper focuses on systemic changes: increasing the accessibility of services, eliminating administrative barriers, and strengthening interagency mechanisms that enable probation to perform not only control functions but also social and legal ones. The study focused on barriers to the integration of previously convicted women (housing, registration, documents, employment, access to services, stigma, and the risk of reoffending) and the legal shortcomings in overcoming them. The final recommendation is that the proposed package of measures—from a unified support route for the first 90 days to the implementation of an interagency risk matrix and domain-specific KPIs—should be launched as an immediate pilot. This will enable the Republic of Kazakhstan to strengthen its compliance with international obligations, including standards for the treatment of women in the criminal justice system (including the principles enshrined in the UN Bangkok Rules), and to transition to a modern, economically rational, and humane justice system in which public safety is achieved through successful social and legal adaptation of individuals, rather than through repeated and costly isolation. ‘This publication was funded by the European Union. https://cabar.asia/en/psychological-supp.body: © CABAR - Central Asian Bureau for Analytical Reporting Please make active links to the source, when using materials from this website На русском Қазақша The publication “Psychological support for parents and guardians raising children with disabilities in Kazakhstan (white paper)” was prepared by Aigerim Kenzhebekova and Aliya Tlegenova with the support of the IWPR Representative Office in Central Asia and the regional analytical platform CABAR.asia. For citation and references to the material, please indicate: Aigerim Kenzhebekova, Aliya Tlegenova, Psychological support for parents and guardians raising children with disabilities in Kazakhstan (white paper) 2026, CABAR.asia. The publication notes that more than 103,000 families in Kazakhstan are raising children with disabilities and special educational needs. These families face chronic stress, emotional burnout, social isolation, and financial overload. According to the first large-scale study conducted by the Mama Pro Foundation for the Support and Development of Socially Vulnerable Women (2025), which included 1,119 parents and guardians, more than half of those surveyed reported a high need for psychological and social support, yet access to it remains extremely limited. International and Kazakhstani experience shows that the lack of systemic support for parents negatively impacts not only their health but also the effectiveness of rehabilitation and educational programs for children themselves. The authors believe that the key challenge in Kazakhstan remains the lack of institutionalized psychological support for parents. The material contains specific recommendations for relevant government agencies, including the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection. Specifically, the authors suggest that psychological support for parents and guardians (individual and group consultations) should be included in individual rehabilitation programs (IRPs) for children as part of a package of guaranteed medical services. Kazakhstan faces a crucial choice: continue to support families with children with disabilities in a fragmented manner or transition to a systemic model of assistance focused on the resilience of the entire family. Incorporating psychological support for parents into government mechanisms will be the first step toward building a comprehensive, equally accessible, and sustainable system. This decision will not only reduce parental burnout but also increase the effectiveness of measures for the rehabilitation and social integration of children. ‘This publication was funded by the European Union. Its contents are the sole responsibility of IWPR and do not necessarily reflect the views of the European Union. © CABAR - Central Asian Bureau for Analytical Reporting Please make active links to the source, when using materials from this website На русском Қазақша The publication “Psychological support for parents and guardians raising children with disabilities in Kazakhstan ” was prepared by Aigerim Kenzhebekova and Aliya Tlegenova with the support of the IWPR Representative Office in Central Asia and the regional analytical platform CABAR.asia. For citation and references to the material, please indicate: Aigerim Kenzhebekova, Aliya Tlegenova, Psychological support for parents and guardians raising children with disabilities in Kazakhstan (policy brief) 2026, CABAR.asia. The publication notes that parents and guardians raising children with disabilities, special needs, or at-risk groups experience chronic stress and emotional burnout. Psychological support for parents and guardians is not prioritized or included in individual rehabilitation programs, psychological and pedagogical correction rooms, psychological, medical, and pedagogical child health services, or other government services. Systematic support for parents as partners in the rehabilitation and care process is lacking. The main problem currently is that the state does not consider the psychological well-being of parents as part of overall support for families with children with disabilities. In Kazakhstan, there are 103,000 families raising children with disabilities, and this does not include families with children with special needs. According to research by international organizations, families with children with special needs experience so-called “disability poverty” (OECD, WHO). Coupled with economic vulnerability, parents and caregivers face disproportionately high levels of parenting stress. Causes range from medical and behavioral factors to social isolation, lack of understanding, and a lack of systemic emotional support. According to a national study conducted by the Mama Pro Foundation (2025), 40% of parents and guardians report constant physical and emotional overload; 73% experience constant worry and anxiety about their child’s future; another 40% regularly experience social isolation, and almost 20% feel permanently lonely. Less than half of respondents receive regular support from their partners. State support, firstly, remains inaccessible (only 15% of respondents are aware of all sources of support), and secondly, lacks a comprehensive approach. International studies show that the higher the degree of unpaid and undistributed care, the higher the risk of poverty, depression, and social isolation in families with children with disabilities. Thus, parents and guardians are left without psychological support, which negatively impacts family resilience, the implementation of inclusive education, and the integration of children into society. International practices demonstrate a wide range of tools for supporting parents of children with disabilities. However, directly adopting these solutions is impossible without taking into account the specifics of Kazakhstan’s social and institutional environment. In conclusion, the authors provide specific recommendations for developing a comprehensive, sustainable support system for families raising children with disabilities. Their implementation will enable the state to transition from a model of “care” to a model of partnership with the family, ensuring compliance with Kazakhstan’s international obligations under the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. ‘This publication was funded by the European Union. Its contents are the sole responsibility of IWPR and do not necessarily reflect the views of the European Union. https://kloop.kg/blog/2026/09/02/my-tsen.body: Facebook Twitter VK Telegram WhatsApp Российский президент Владимир Путин поблагодарил главу Кыргызстана Садыра Жапарова за поддержку русского языка. « Мы очень ценим Ваше внимание к вопросам поддержки русского языка, имеющего в республике статус официального », — сказал Путин и напомнил о строительстве девяти русскоязычных школ, три из которых должны начать работу в 2027 году. Поддержка кыргызского языка Кыргызстан утвердил государственный язык в 1989 году. В 2000 году русскому языку дали статус официального. В 2023 году власти Кыргызстана приняли закон о госязыке. инициировал законопроект Кабинет министров, разрабатывала – Нацкомиссия по госязыку. И это вызвало бурную и негативную реакцию у российских политиков и СМИ. Свое право на усиление госязыка республике пришлось отстаивать на уровне президента – Садыр Жапаров публично вступал в полемику с главой российского МИД Сергеем Лавровым, который назвал закон о госязыке «недемократичным». Как российские чиновники и федеральные СМИ, так и некоторые кыргызские политики и общественные деятели считали, что этот закон якобы притесняет русский язык. Им оппонировал глава Нацкомиссии по государственному языку и языковой политике Каныбек Осмоналиев, который отмечал, что в законе нет норм, преследующих русский язык. Российские политики болезненно реагировали на события в Кыргызстане, которые вообще никак не связаны с внешней политикой России – например, на идею изменить названия районов Бишкека, которые остались еще со времен Советского Союза. Депутатка российской Госдумы Светлана Журова считала , что такая инициатива приведет к ущемлению прав русскоговорящего населения Кыргызстана и пугала «украинским сценарием». «Украинским сценарием» в Кыргызстане пугали не только российские политики и пропагандисты, но и центральноазиатские пророссийские СМИ и каналы. Они тоже были против принятия закона о госязыке . Освещали законопроект и российские СМИ. «Ведомости», например, увидели в нем «западный след». Научный сотрудник Берлинского центра Карнеги Темур Умаров считал, что обостренная реакция российской политэлиты на новый закон в Кыргызстане вызвана «искаженным представлением», о том, как должны себя вести бывшие части СССР и Российской империи. «Для них успех российской внешней политики – это если в мире, и вокруг России в первую очередь, есть представление о том, что существует такой “русский мир”, в котором роль России незыблема и первична. Роль русского языка тоже никем не оспаривается, и на нем говорят все граждане стран, которые в этот “русский мир” входят. Таким образом они демонстрируют всему миру, что Россия все еще является великой державой», – рассуждал он. Эксперт считал, что российское влияние в регионе тоже постепенно уменьшается. И для того, чтобы этого не произошло, России нужно было строить бесплатные русские школы, демонстрировать привлекательность русского языка и русской культуры. Отчасти Россия и решила пойти этим путем. Она строит в Кыргызстане девять русскоязычных школ – по одной в каждой из семи областей Кыргызстана, плюс в Бишкеке и Оше. https://www.osce.org/chairpersonship/667.body: Press release 134th Incident Prevention and Response Mechanism meeting takes place in Ergneti Date: 8 September 2026 Place: ERGNETI Source: OSCE Chairpersonship ERGNETI, 8 September 2026 – The 134th Incident Prevention and Response Mechanism (IPRM) meeting took place today in Ergneti. The meeting was co-facilitated by Christoph Späti, Special Representative of the OSCE Chairperson-in-Office for the South Caucasus, and Jaana Napa, Deputy Head of the EU Monitoring Mission in Georgia (EUMM). The EUMM and OSCE co-facilitators welcomed the continued commitment of all participants to the IPRM format and reiterated its importance as a practical platform for addressing security-related developments and matters impacting conflict-affected communities on both sides of the administrative boundary line (ABL). While recognizing that limitation to freedom of movement remained, the co-facilitators welcomed more frequent opening of crossing points along the ABL. They underlined that greater opportunities for cross-ABL movement can improve the daily lives, livelihoods and sense of security of conflict-affected women, men and children, and encouraged further steps towards the full reopening of the crossing points. Detention cases remained an important part of the discussions. The EUMM and OSCE reiterated their concern over continued detentions and called for a humanitarian approach to resolving all existing cases. Participants also positively assessed the irrigation season and exchanged views on practical issues related to access to irrigation water for communities on both sides of the ABL. The co-facilitators encouraged further progress through continued engagement and reiterated their readiness to support efforts to address irrigation-related challenges. All participants reaffirmed the key role of the EUMM-managed Hotline in facilitating the timely exchange of information and contributing to stability along the ABL. The Hotline continued to address a range of practical, security and humanitarian issues, including detentions, “borderisation” and socio-economic issues. The participants agreed to hold the next regular IPRM meeting on 22 October 2026. https://skopje.osce.org/news/mission-sko.body: News News Item New protocol brings faster access to identity, rights, and services for all Issued on: 28 April 2026 Issued by: OSCE Mission to Skopje Fields of work: Human rights , Roma and Sinti North Macedonia is a global champion in ending statelessness. The country introduces measures to prevent future cases. The OSCE Mission to Skopje, jointly with the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Ministry of Health promoted a new Protocol on Procedures for Statelessness. The Protocol sets clear steps for institutions to work together to prevent new cases, because not having a legal identity means not being able to see a doctor, go to school, or access basic services. The event brought together representatives from key institutions, civil society organizations, and professionals who work directly with people at risk of statelessness. It also recognized the efforts of frontline staff who helped resolve real-life cases and improve co-ordination between institutions. “This is about real people and real lives. This Protocol helps ensure that every child born is registered, every person is recognized, and everyone can access their basic rights.”, said the Head of the OSCE Mission in to Skopje, Ambassador Kilian Wahl. The initiative sustains recent progress. Already by mid-2025, North Macedonia had resolved all known cases linked to the breakup of the former Yugoslavia, granting citizenship to 317 people. However, challenges remain, especially for children born to parents without regulated legal status. A recent pilot effort showed how co-operation can make a difference. In one case, institutions worked together to ensure that both a mother and her newborn received personal documents and access to healthcare, quickly and effectively. The new Protocol aims to make such solutions standard practice. The OSCE Mission continues to support national authorities and partners in preventing and reducing statelessness, ensuring that everyone can enjoy their fundamental rights and that no one is left behind. https://www.osce.org/chairpersonship/667.body: Press release From Geneva to Helsinki and beyond: significance of the OSCE’s founding legacy and its future at the heart of the third Chair conference Date: 3 September 2026 Place: BERN Source: OSCE Chairpersonship , OSCE Secretariat BERN, 3 September 2026 – Fifty-one years after the Helsinki Final Act was adopted, the Swiss OSCE Chairpersonship and Dodis Research centre (Swiss Diplomatic Documents) brought together political leaders, diplomats, historians and experts in Bern to reflect on the origins of the Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe (CSCE) and the relevance of its founding principles for European security today and tomorrow. The high-level segment of the Chairpersonship’s conference, “From Geneva to Helsinki: Founding Process and Core Purpose of the OSCE” , was held today at the University of Bern as part of the conference of the International Committee of Editors of Diplomatic Documents (ICEDD). The event is the third of four thematic conferences organized by the Swiss OSCE Chairpersonship in 2026. The discussions, drawing on the expertise of the Dodis research centre, revisited the diplomatic process that led from the preparatory consultations in Geneva to the adoption of the Helsinki Final Act in 1975. The conference explored the broader significance of the Helsinki Final Act, principles its enduring continued relevance of the OSCE’s comprehensive approach to security. Against the backdrop of today’s security challenges, participants also looked beyond the historical record, exploring how the Helsinki legacy continues to influence diplomacy, dialogue and co-operation in a changing European security landscape. OSCE Chairman-in-Office, Federal Councillor Ignazio Cassis, underlined that the history of the Helsinki Process offers lessons that remain highly relevant in today’s fractured geopolitical environment: ”Co-operation does not require agreement. It requires the willingness to keep talking despite disagreement. The Helsinki Final Act was not signed between friends. It was signed between adversaries. We do not know what European security will look like in five or ten years. Nor do we know when the next opportunity for diplomacy will come. But we can make sure that, when it comes, there is still a table around which everyone can sit. That is not nostalgia for Helsinki. It is preparation for what comes next”. OSCE Secretary General Feridun H. Sinirlioğlu highlighted the continued importance of the Organization’s founding purpose: “Globally and in Europe, we have reached once again a critical juncture. The geopolitical landscape has changed. But one thing has not changed, and will not change. Geography. That is why, fifty years ago, countries recognized the need for an inclusive security platform - the OSCE. We still need that platform today, and we will need it for the years to come,” said OSCE Secretary General Feridun H. Sinirlioğlu. Prof. Dr. Sacha Zala, Director of Dodis, presented the largest joint edition of diplomatic documents on the origins of the CSCE CSCE Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe /OSCE, bringing together primary sources from 15 countries and two international organizations. This forward-looking dimension is central to the Swiss Chairpersonship, which has placed at the heart of its priorities the Helsinki Principles for lasting peace, inclusive multilateral diplomacy, anticipating technologies, democracy and human rights, as well as the OSCE’s ability to act. Media advisory From Geneva to Helsinki: What the OSCE’s founding legacy means for European security today and tomorrow Date: 27 August 2026 Place: VIENNA/BERN Source: OSCE Chairpersonship VIENNA/BERN, 27 August 2026 – The Chairpersonship’s Conference on “From Geneva to Helsinki: Founding Process and Core Purpose of the OSCE” , to be held in Bern on 3 –4 September 2026, is the third of four thematic conferences organized by the Swiss OSCE Chairpersonship this year. The event takes place as part of the conference of the International Committee of Editors of Diplomatic Documents (ICEDD) and constitutes a high-level segment bringing together historians, editors of diplomatic documents, diplomats and political representatives. The conference focuses on the early phase of the Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe (CSCE), from the preparatory consultations in Geneva to the adoption of the Helsinki Final Act in 1975. By revisiting the diplomatic processes and negotiations that shaped this milestone of Cold War diplomacy, the conference aims to highlight how participating States developed a framework for dialogue, confidence-building and co-operation across political divides. At a time when the principles and mechanisms of co-operative security are being tested by profound geopolitical challenges, the conference will also explore the continued relevance of the Helsinki legacy and its implications for the future role of the OSCE as a platform for dialogue and stability across the OSCE region. The high-level segment of the conference, to be held at the University of Bern, will feature addresses by the OSCE Chairman-in-Office, Federal Councillor Ignazio Cassis, and OSCE Secretary General Feridun H. Sinirlioğlu, alongside distinguished historians, diplomats and experts. The event will be open to media representatives. Media representatives are required to obtain accreditation in advance. Interested journalists are invited to register no later than Monday, 31 August 2026, at 12:00 (CET) via the following link . Further information about the conference is available here . https://bih.osce.org/news/mission-bosnia.body: News News Item Responsibility Must Prevail Over Division and Provocation Issued on: 1 September 2026 Issued by: OSCE Mission to Bosnia and Herzegovina Fields of work: Rule of law SARAJEVO, 01 September 2026 – The OSCE Mission to Bosnia and Herzegovina (the Mission) strongly condemns any threats, intimidation and targeting of public officials, journalists and their family members, and warns that increasingly inflammatory public discourse risks further undermining public safety, democratic participation and media freedom. Such threats are unacceptable. They constitute a direct attack on democratic participation, freedom of the media and the right to live free from fear and intimidation. Threats, intimidation, harassment or other pressure against journalists and media organizations, including online, must be promptly and effectively addressed by the competent authorities. Those responsible must be held accountable in accordance with the law. Similarly, while criticism of public officials’ policy statements is a legitimate part of democratic discourse, threats of violence, whether direct or implied, against public officials are unacceptable, undemocratic, and may constitute a criminal offence. We urge political leaders at every level to refrain from any rhetoric that further inflames tensions and to take active steps to de-escalate the situation. Citizens deserve leaders who choose responsibility over provocation, and dialogue over division. We call on all institutions responsible for public order and the rule of law to act swiftly and impartially to protect those under threat and to prevent and sanction any incitement to hatred or violence. This includes conduct such as the denial of adjudicated atrocities or the glorification of persons found guilty of genocide, crimes against humanity or war crimes, where such conduct amounts to incitement. The Mission strongly condemns the glorification of individuals convicted of genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes. As the Mission stressed in its 28 August statement “ Respect Victims, Don’t Glorify Perpetrators ,” those entrusted with public office have a particular responsibility not to use their influence to deepen divisions or cause further pain to victims and survivors. Respect for judicially established facts, the dignity of victims, freedom of expression and the safety of every individual are not competing principles. They are essential foundations of a democratic society and of lasting peace and reconciliation in Bosnia and Herzegovina. https://kloop.kg/blog/2026/09/11/finanso.body: Facebook Twitter VK Telegram WhatsApp 826,7 млн сомов — нарушения на такую сумму выявила Счетная палата в бюджете Балыкчы. Городом руководит, он родственник управделами президента Каныбека Туманбаева Баатырбек Жантаев. Сам Жантаев утверждает, что у него «все прозрачно». Счетная палата провела аудит бюджета Балыкчы на период с 1 января 2024 года по 31 декабря 2025 года. Общая сумма обнаруженных финансовых нарушений — 826, 7 млн сомов. Сообщается, что 776 млн «подлежат возмещению» и 425 млн сомов уже восстановлено. Список нарушений, указанных Счетной палатой, обширный, в том числе недопоступление средств в бюджет и нецелевое использования средств. Баатырбек Жантаев утверждает, что «процедурные нарушения выдают за коррупцию», а ему «нечего скрывать, все прозрачно». «Аудит Счетной палаты КР охватывает период 2024-2025 гг. Пытаться переложить финансовые отчеты и решения прежнего руководства на текущую работу — преднамеренная провокация», — считает Жантаев. По его словам, «основная часть сумм в отчете — это технические ошибки прошлых лет, которые уже исправлены, а также плановый учет имущества города». Жантаев настаивает, что у него «нулевая толерантность к нарушениям». « Если бы я допустил хоть один факт коррупции — я готов нести личную ответственность перед народом и законом по всей строгости », — говорит он. Хотя Жантаев настаивает, что в аудите Счетной палаты ошибки прежнего руководства города — с 2024 по 31 декабря 2025 года — он лукавит. Президент Садыр Жапаров назначил Жантаева мэром Балыкчы 14 июля 2025 года — то есть в отчете есть период и за полгода его работы в руководстве города. До мэрства Жантаев был начальником отдела материально-технического обеспечения «Кыргыз темир жолу». Хотя Жантаев в своих ответах пытается создать себе образ некоего борца с коррупцией, до мэрства он был фигурантом журналистских расследований. Жантаев приходится Туманбаеву двоюродным братом по материнской линии (бөлө). До этого Жантаев был больше известен как доверенное лицо Туманбаева. Жантаев упоминался в расследовании OCCRP, Temirov Live и «Клоопа» о том, как большие госпроекты достались подставным людям из окружения президента Кыргызстана. В материале говорилось, что некоторые из важнейших государственных проектов отдали под реализацию компаниям, подотчетным людям из окружения Туманбаева, а иногда и близким самого Жапарова. Также про Жантаева писал «Азаттык» в своём расследовании о том, что Туманбаев связан со стройкой нового Белого дома в Бишкеке. Тогда журналисты отмечали, что Жантаева можно заметить на многих объектах, которые строит государство, а некоторые компании, в которых руководителем был Туманбаев перешли впоследствии под управление Жантаева. Кроме того, Жантаев упоминался в расследовании Factcheck.kg о коррупции на госпредприятии «Кыргыз темир жолу». ЭТО МОЖЕТ БЫТЬ ИНТЕРЕСНО ЕЩЕ ОТ АВТОРА Медведь в объятиях дракона. https://kloop.kg/blog/2026/09/11/kara-su.body: Facebook Twitter VK Telegram WhatsApp Рынок Кара-Суу, Туратали В распоряжение Управделами президента передают очередной крупный объект. На этот раз — второй по величине после «Дордоя» рынок Кыргызстана, расположенный на юге страны, более известный как Кара-Сууйский рынок или рынок «Туратали». Передачу рынка Управделами президента изданию «Турмуш» подтвердил его бывший директор Нурбек Эргешов. По его словам, процесс передачи базара начался 2-3 месяца назад. «Сейчас процесс приема рынка еще не завершен. Уже три месяца мы никак не можем окончательно его передать», — рассказал он «Турмушу». Точные причины передачи рынка в ведение Управделами неизвестны. При этом в апреле этого года во время рабочей поездки в Ошскую область президент Кыргызстана Садыр Жапаров пообещал местным жителям, что на Кара-Сууйском рынке построят современный торговый центр. Тогда он ничего не говорил о передаче базара в ведение Управделами, но раскритиковал местных чиновников за медленную модернизацию рынка и привел в пример улучшение условий для торговцев Ошского рынка в Бишкеке. Модернизацию базара в столице как раз курирует Управделами президента и его глава Каныбек Туманбаев — ярчайший кадр Жапарова. Каныбек Туманбаев Журналисты «Клоопа» и Temirov Live в июле обнаружили , что у Туманбаева есть действующее российское гражданство. Это нарушает сразу три закона Кыргызстана — люди с двойным гражданством не имеют права занимать руководящие должности в госорганах. Президент до сих пор никак на это не отреагировал, и продолжает передавать в ведение Управделами все новые объекты. Сейчас под управлением Туманбаева уже более 30 подведомственных организаций. Кара-Сууйский рынок — крупный торговый узел на юге страны. Здесь пересекаются пути из Китая, Узбекистана и Таджикистана. Рынок возник еще в восьмидесятых, когда советская власть открыла в Кара-Суу колхозный базар. В девяностых, после развала СССР, его перенесли за город, где он оброс новыми рядами. Контролировали его десятки частных управляющих — базаркомов. Многие из них были в прошлом госслужащими или выходцами из кругов кругов. В январе 2024 года тогдашний глава ГКНБ Камчыбек Ташиев заявил во время встречи с торговцами, что рынок перейдет в ведение государства. Дальше началась национализация рынка, которую некоторые сотрудники базара и владельцы торговых точек назвали «рейдерским захватом». Руководить новым рынком, по указанию президента Жапарова, поставили Нурбека Эргешова. Торговцы не раз жаловались на беспредел со стороны руководства рынка и базаркома Эргешова. По словам торговцев, территории базара ему было недостаточно и вскоре он начал претендовать и на прилегающую территорию, находящуюся в частной собственности. Участки отобрали у владельцев через суд и снесли буквально за один день. Нурбек Эргешов А в 2025 году Эргешов избил одного из торговцев. Тогда, в конце июня предприниматель Исламбек Халилов решил продать свой контейнер и пошел к базаркому согласовать сделку. Но тот потребовал долю от стоимости контейнера. А после отказа Эргешов начал бить Халилова по голове кулаком и телефоном. ЭТО МОЖЕТ БЫТЬ ИНТЕРЕСНО ЕЩЕ ОТ АВТОРА Медведь в объятиях дракона. В отличие от южной и центральной частей Аркадага, которые застраивались на свободной от прежнего жилья территории (хотя, как ранее отметил «Метеожурнал», ради города вырубили 300 гектаров садов и виноградников), в северной его части располагается село Горджав, и план строительства предусматривает его снос. В северной части нового города находится село, которое нужно уничтожить, чтобы завершить проект Как рассказал побывавший в селе корреспондент «Хроники Туркменистана», жители Горджава уже начали разбирать дома на стройматериалы, которые тут же продают или вывозят, чтобы использовать позже. По некоторым данным, проживающим в селе жителям предоставят жилье в Аркадаге, но когда и на каких условиях, пока неясно. Ранее корреспонденты ХТ отметили , что город на данный момент не заселен, по крайней мере часть жилых домов еще не доделана. https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-poland-b.body: News Trump Tells Kyiv To Stop Attacks On Russian Diesel As Moscow's Drones Strike Near Polish Border By RFE/RL September 13, 2026 12:26 CET Updated September 13, 2026 21:03 CET Trump Tells Kyiv To Stop Attacks On Russian Diesel As Moscow's Drones Strike Near Polish Border Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google US President Donald Trump speaks to reporters aboard Air Force One on his return to the United States following a visit to Ireland. US President Donald Trump has called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop targeting Russian diesel infrastructure amid Russia's relentless attacks across Ukraine, including near the Polish border. "There are plenty of other targets. Don't hit diesel fuel," Trump told reporters on September 13 during his visit to Ireland. "You have to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia," he said. Trump's comment came a week after his envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, had visited Kyiv and Moscow in the latest US-mediated diplomatic effort to bring the wartime capitals closer to a negotiated agreement. While all sides have called the talks "substantial," the dynamics on the front line have not changed, with Russia continuing to attack Ukraine and hitting its civilian, logistics, and energy infrastructure as the cold weather sets in. Ukraine, meanwhile, has continued to respond, targeting energy and military sites inside Russia with its long-range drone attacks. Kyiv has been calling the effort "long-range sanctions" as it seeks to curb Moscow's energy profits and force it to negotiate. Since the beginning of the summer, Ukrainian drone strikes have caused nationwide fuel shortages in Russia and stoked discontent among its citizens, who were disconnected from the war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year. SEE ALSO: Ukraine's Refinery Attacks Force Russia To Turn Abroad To Process Its Oil Ukraine Warns Russia 'Knocking On NATO's Door' With the latest diplomatic efforts yielding no practical easing of tensions on the battlefield, two Russian drone strikes hit near the Polish border early on September 13. The first strike hit a petrol station near the Yahodyn border crossing between Poland and Ukraine, in the latter's Volyn region. No casualties were reported. The second, also in Volyn, struck the locomotive of a passenger train just two kilometers from the Polish border, Ukraine's state railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsia, reported. According to Oleksandr Shevchenko, a local transportation official, the train was traveling from Kyiv to Warsaw. As Ukrzaliznytsia said that a threat-monitoring group was able to warn the train's crew of the attack in advance, no casualties were reported. Video footage spread over Ukrainian social media showed people running from the blast at the railway station. Embed share Tusk Says Poland On High Alert After Russian Strikes Near Ukraine's Western Border by RFE/RL Embed share The code has been copied to your clipboard. width px height px The URL has been copied to your clipboard No media source currently available 0:00 0:01:47 0:00 Separately, Ukrzaliznytsia said that "quite possibly," the original target of the drone strike could have been the "diplomatic train," which carried top European officials, including former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson. It added that former CIA Director David Petraeus was aboard another train at the time. Petraeus told The New York Times that he could hear Russian drones above and then an explosion, leading to the immediate evacuation of passengers. "For those who have not been under fire, this was terrifying...This is the act of a truly barbaric leader trying to terrorize Ukrainian civilians," Petraeus said. As the incidents occurred, air-raid alerts were issued in several eastern districts of Poland. While there were no reports of violations of Polish airspace, Jacek Goryszewski, spokesman for the Operational Command of the Polish Armed Forces, said the "threat to Poland was real." In separate incidents on September 13, Romanian authorities reported a drone entering the country, and Lithuania called on residents in the capital and neighboring regions to preventively seek shelter after issuing an alert of possible drone sighting. The country's main airport in Vilnius was shut down and NATO jets were scrambled. The alert was called off within an hour. "Russia's barbaric strikes at the Ukraine-Poland border in Yahodyn are not just a continuation of its attacks on our state borders," Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha wrote on X on September 13. "This is Putin's terror 'knocking' directly on the doors of the EU and NATO." He urged European leaders to "throw the full weight" of sanctions against Russia. SEE ALSO: Russian Strikes Kill 9 Across Ukraine, As Zelenskyy Offers To Meet Putin At Miami G20 Earlier this month, Germany officially blamed an incident on Moscow in which explosive-laden drones interrupted flights at Leipzig Airport. At the time, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said that "Europeans are faced with a hard truth that this is the new normal." "It is precisely to prevent these strikes from spreading further into Europe that Ukrainian men and women fight every single day, laying down their lives to keep this aggression from expanding," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a post on Telegram on September 13. "Russian terrorism is a shared threat to many, but it can and must be defeated right here in Ukraine," he added. According to Zelenskyy, a total of 2,100 drones, 1,700 gliding bombs, and 73 missiles were launched at targets across Ukraine in the past week. Ukrainian authorities said that elsewhere in Ukraine, the latest Russian attacks had also targeted the country's western regions of Ivano-Frankivsk, Ternopil, and Lviv, as well as the war-torn eastern Donetsk region and the key southern region of Odesa. SEE ALSO: Ukrainian Soldier Honored For Rescue In 'Kill Zone' Regional authorities in the Odesa region said nine people had been injured after a drone struck several residential buildings. A warehouse in the region was also reportedly targeted. Meanwhile, in the region's capital city of Odesa, rescuers have completed work at the site of the drone strike on a 25-story residential building on the night of September 12. Two people were killed and more than 20 injured in that attack. Russia's Defense Ministry claimed that its overnight strikes targeted "logistics centers through which military cargo is delivered and distributed, as well as energy facilities that support their operation." The ministry also reported strikes on railway infrastructure in western Ukraine. Russia denies targeting civilian areas despite widespread evidence of such attacks that have killed thousands of people since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion. https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-sees-rus.body: News Analysis Ukraine Sees Russian-Iranian Sanctions Networks Converging As US Targets Tankers By Alex Raufoglu September 11, 2026 14:57 CET Ukraine Sees Russian-Iranian Sanctions Networks Converging As US Targets Tankers Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google The M/T Charminar tanker, one of five Iran-linked crude oil tankers reportedly rendered inoperable by US strikes on September 8. (file photo) WASHINGTON -- The recent US destruction of five Iranian oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz has exposed more than the widening confrontation between Washington and Tehran. It has highlighted an increasingly intertwined sanctions-evasion system linking Iran and Russia -- a network of ships, managers, intermediaries, and trading routes that Ukrainian officials and US sanctions experts say the West can no longer treat as two separate problems. Three of the five tankers -- Kaviz, Charminar, and Riesco -- had direct links to Russia’s shadow oil fleet, according to Vladyslav Vlasiuk, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s sanctions commissioner. All three transported Russian oil and called at Russian ports, Vlasiuk told RFE/RL on September 10. Riesco, he said, carried both Russian and Iranian oil and participated in ship-to-ship transfers involving other sanctioned vessels. “Russia and Iran have a long history of cooperation, and their sanctions-evasion networks increasingly overlap,” Vlasiuk said. SEE ALSO: From Russia With Expertise: Iranian Students Return Home With Potentially Deadly Knowledge Of Drones, AI, And More Philip Luck, director of the Economics Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies and a former deputy chief economist at the US State Department, described the system more bluntly: “There’s not a Russian shadow fleet and Iranian shadow fleet. There’s one shadow fleet that is facilitating Iranian oil sales and Russian oil sales.” Tankers Tied To Moscow Kaviz operated between the Russian ports of Ust-Luga and Novorossiysk and had a history of switching off its automatic identification system, which allows authorities and other vessels to track ships. Vlasiuk linked it to Fractal Marine DMCC, a network involved in moving Russian oil after Western sanctions were imposed. Charminar repeatedly called at Russian ports, including Ust-Luga, Primorsk, Vysotsk, and St. Petersburg. Vlasiuk said it was connected to a shipping network controlled by Iranian oil businessman Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani. After Britain sanctioned Fractal Marine, vessels connected to the network were transferred to other managers while their Russian oil operations continued, Vlasiuk said. SEE ALSO: US Sanctions All Remaining Iranian Airlines In Sweeping Aviation Crackdown Riesco illustrates the two-way nature of the trade. It carried both Russian and Iranian oil and participated in ship-to-ship transfers involving other sanctioned vessels. All three tankers are sanctioned by Ukraine and the United States, according to Vlasiuk. Kaviz is also sanctioned by the European Union, Britain, Canada, and Switzerland. Vlasiuk did not estimate how much revenue the vessels generated for Russia. Their importance, he said, lies in helping Russian oil reach global markets despite Western restrictions. “These vessels were part of the infrastructure that enabled Russian oil to keep reaching the global market despite sanctions, allowing Russia to preserve a major source of revenue,” he said. For Ukraine, that infrastructure is itself a target. “The same vessels, masters, managers, intermediaries and shipping routes are used to transport both Russian and Iranian oil,” Vlasiuk said. One Fleet, Two Oil Trades Luck said the implications extend beyond the three ships because Russia and Iran sell oil to many of the same markets. That creates a challenge for sanctions policymakers: measures aimed at one country’s oil trade may affect the other because the logistics are shared. “So anything, if you want to put more pressure on Iran, you’re gonna be putting more pressure on Russia,” Luck said. “And if you put more pressure on Russia, you’re putting more pressure on Iran. It’s the exact same problem.” The issue has become more urgent as Washington combines economic pressure on Tehran with direct military action. The US says the Iranian tankers were part of a shadow network helping finance Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and its proxies. The strikes followed Iranian attacks on US naval forces, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has warned that Washington will respond to further attacks. SEE ALSO: US Targets Turkish Bank In New Bid To Cut Iran's Financial Lifelines The confrontation has also increased pressure on energy markets. Washington and Tehran are seeking influence over the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of global oil supplies passed before the war. For Kyiv, the tanker strikes show why maritime networks have become an increasingly important sanctions target. “As long as this infrastructure remains operational, opportunities to evade sanctions will remain,” Vlasiuk said. Ukraine Sees A Wider Russia-Iran Link The episode comes as Washington considers expanding its ability to target Russia’s energy revenues and the networks helping Moscow evade sanctions. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 passed the Senate on August 7 by 86-11. It targets Russia’s shadow fleet, imposes additional sanctions on Russian officials and financial institutions, and authorizes the president to impose duties of up to 100 percent on goods from major purchasers of Russian oil and gas and countries involved in sanctions evasion. It also extends the Iran Sanctions Act for five years. The bill’s future in the House remains uncertain, but Ukraine says it could provide leverage against Russia, whose energy revenues remain central to financing the war. At a September 10 briefing hosted by the Bipartisan Congressional Ukraine Caucus, Ukraine’s Charge d’Affaires in Washington, Denys Sienik, urged lawmakers to view the measure as a source of leverage rather than a finished instrument. “All the decisions, major decisions, indeed require compromise,” Sienik said. He warned that Russia continues earning substantial oil and gas revenues while producing weapons and recruiting soldiers. “What message will it send to Ukrainians, and what message will it send to Russia if this does not pass?” he asked. Former State Department sanctions coordinator Daniel Fried offered a similar assessment. “If the US authority would increase diplomacy to end Russia’s war against Ukraine, it should increase the leverage it’s using against Russia,” he said. “Now is the time to use it.” Fried cited the Obama administration’s Iran policy, when Congress pressured the administration to threaten countries buying Iranian oil while allowing waivers for nations that significantly reduced purchases over six-month periods. China and India protested but ultimately reduced their imports. He said the current bill could likewise give Washington room to negotiate with major buyers rather than automatically impose maximum penalties. Fried acknowledged questions about how the bill’s thresholds would be calculated and how authorities would determine the destination of Russian oil. “But with this bill, if it passes, there is something to work with,” he said. “There is leverage. If it doesn’t pass, there is nothing, zero.” Fried said sanctions need not eliminate every barrel of Russian or Iranian oil from global markets. Their goal is to reduce the revenue available to sustain war. Forcing Russia to sell at lower prices, he said, can also reduce money flowing to the Kremlin. That approach places the shadow fleet at the center of the sanctions debate. https://www.rferl.org/a/iran-us-oil-ship.body: Iran US, Iran Trade Strikes On Shipping As Oil Prices Surge Above $100 A Barrel By RFE/RL September 09, 2026 17:29 CET Updated September 09, 2026 21:47 CET US, Iran Trade Strikes On Shipping As Oil Prices Surge Above $100 A Barrel Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google US Destroys IRGC Oil Tankers After Iran Targets US Navy Warships (loop video) Iran said it attacked vessels near the Strait of Hormuz on September 9 after the United States destroyed several Iranian oil tankers overnight, in a sharp escalation in the six-month war. The tit-for-tat strikes led to a surge in global oil prices, with Brent crude reaching $100 per barrel for the first time since July. Tehran also said it had fired ballistic missiles at a US base in Jordan. No casualties or damage were reported. Iran and the United States have been engaged in tit-for-tat strikes in the past few weeks, in a move that observers say could reignite a full-blown war. US President Donald Trump said on September 9 that the United States was not looking for a deal to end the war, although he added that negotiations could happen. Trump also told reporters that he believes that the conflict will end “immediately” after the midterm elections in November because Iran “can't hold out any longer.” SEE ALSO: Trump Downplays Report China Aided Tehran In Attack On US Troops In Jordan Targeting Shipping The US military said it sank five Iranian oil tankers overnight near Kharg Island, Iran’s main oil export hub, calling it a response to Tehran firing missiles at a US Navy warship over the past two days. Iran retaliated by firing 20 ballistic missiles toward Jordan, which said it intercepted 18 of them. Jordan said two of the missiles landed in unpopulated areas. The Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC), the elite branch of Iran’s armed forces, claimed that it also attacked two US vessels, eight oil tankers, and 10 “noncompliant vessels” that were trying to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. A key artery for global energy supplies, the strategic waterway has been effectively closed by Tehran since the start of the war with the United States in February. Earlier in the war, Iran established a shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz that hugged the Iranian coastline. It said any vessels using a US-backed route along Oman’s coast would be targeted. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), which is affiliated with the British Navy, said on September 9 that “several” vessels in the Gulf of Oman and the Persian Gulf were “subject to disabling fire as part of ongoing military activity in the region.” Embed share Tehran Targets US Base In Jordan After Iranian Oil Tankers Sunk by RFE/RL Embed share The code has been copied to your clipboard. width px height px The URL has been copied to your clipboard No media source currently available 0:00 0:00:53 0:00 Separately, the IRGC warned tanker crews in ports in Kuwait and Bahrain, both US allies, to evacuate, raising fears of further disruption around the Strait of Hormuz. The escalation has already affected shipping: data from Kpler, a commodities and shipping analytics company, showed only six commercial vessels crossed the strait on September 8, well below the recent average. Also on September 9, the IRGC for the first time added parts of the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea to a new "prohibited zone" where vessels will be subject to “sanctions.” US Warns Iran Will 'Lose Tankers' Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned the US attack on its oil tankers as “an overt threat to regional and international peace and security,” saying that they "increase the dangers of tensions in the region.” SEE ALSO: US Sanctions All Remaining Iranian Airlines In Sweeping Aviation Crackdown US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Iran would “lose tankers” every time it attempted to hit US ships. "Iran continues to try to hit US naval ships, and for every time they do that or try to do that, they're going to lose tankers, and I think you'll see that again today," Rubio told reporters on September 8 on a visit to Colombia. Rubio's remarks came as Washington intensified its campaign to squeeze Iran economically. The United States announced new sanctions on September 8 targeting Iran's aviation sector and companies accused of helping Tehran obtain aircraft and sensitive technology. On the same day, Iran's national currency, the rial, fell to a new low against major foreign currencies. The United States has also imposed a naval blockade on Iranian vessels and ports, disrupting Iran’s oil exports, its key source of revenue.
