https://www.fararu.com/fa/news/1001997/%.body: ژنرال دن کین در «۶۰ Minutes» میگوید تصویر هلیکوپتر نجات افسر تسلیحات اف-۱۵ عمداً محو شده، چون نوع آن محرمانه است. اما بررسی جزئیات عملیات نشان میدهد آنچه واشنگتن پنهان میکند احتمالاً نوع هلیکوپتر نیست؛ بلکه مدل دقیق، پیکربندی و فناوریهایی است که آن را قادر کرد به برنامه عملیات نجات در ایران اضافه شود و براوو را بیرون بکشد. پ ، پـ تبلیغات تبلیغات فرارو- یک لحظه کوتاه در مستند «60 Minutes» شاید از تمام تصاویر عملیات نجات دو خدمه اف-۱۵ئی آمریکا در ایران مهمتر باشد. تصاویر نجات «دود ۴۴ براوو»، افسر تسلیحات جنگنده سرنگونشده، پخش میشود؛ اما هلیکوپتری که برای بیرون کشیدن او از دل کوهستان ایران وارد عمل شده، عمداً محو شده است. به گزارش فرارو، مجری از ژنرال دن کین، رئیس ستاد مشترک ارتش آمریکا، میپرسد چرا تصویر هلیکوپتر را تار کردهاند. پاسخ کین کوتاه است: نمیخواهیم نوع هلیکوپتر مشخص شود؛ این اطلاعات محرمانه است. تصاویر محو شده از هلیکوپتر نجات افسر تسلیحات جنگنده اف 15 در ایران اما یک مشکل وجود دارد: چند ماه قبل، مقامهای آمریکایی و رسانههای تخصصی عملاً گفته بودند که این پرندهها «Little Bird» بودهاند. گزارش رسمی مجله تخصصی Air & Space Forces نیز از سه هلیکوپتر کوچک و بسیار قدرتمندی خبر میدهد که برای عملیات نجات براوو به داخل ایران منتقل شدند و به احتمال بسیار زیاد همان خانواده «Little Bird» بودند. پس اگر نام «Little Bird» دیگر راز نیست، چرا ژنرال کین هنوز نمیخواهد تصویر هلیکوپتر دیده شود؟ از یک اف-۱۵ سرنگونشده تا فرود در قلب ایران ماجرا از سوم آوریل ۲۰۲۶ آغاز شد؛ زمانی که اف-۱۵ئی «Dude 44» در جریان عملیات بر فراز ایران سرنگون شد و هر دو خدمه آن، خلبان «Alpha» و افسر تسلیحات «Bravo»، با ایجکت از جنگنده جدا شدند. آلفا در همان ساعات نخست پیدا شد. برای نجات او، نیرویی شامل ۲۱ فروند هواپیما و هلیکوپتر وارد حریم ایران شد؛ آ-۱۰ها برای پشتیبانی نزدیک، هواپیماهای HC-130J برای هماهنگی و سوخترسانی و هلیکوپترهای HH-60W Jolly Green II برای انتقال خدمه به کار گرفته شدند. عملیات حدود هفت ساعت و آن هم در روشنایی روز ادامه داشت. یکی از آ-۱۰ها هدف آتش قرار گرفت و یک هلیکوپتر نجات نیز چندین گلوله خورد. اما براوو داستان دیگری داشت. او نزدیک به ۴۸ ساعت در کوهستانهای زاگرس مخفی ماند، در حالی که نیروهای ایرانی به دنبال او بودند. سرانجام محل او شناسایی شد و آمریکا عملیات دوم، بسیار بزرگتر و پیچیدهتری را آغاز کرد. طبق توضیحات منتشرشده، این بار دو فروند هواپیمای ترابری MC-130J در یک نوار خاکی موقت در داخل ایران فرود آمدند. از درون آنها هلیکوپترهای بسیار کوچک «Little Bird» خارج و در زمانی کوتاه آماده پرواز شدند. سپس همین پرندههای کوچک به سمت خطالرأس کوهستانی رفتند تا براوو را پیدا و منتقل کنند. این انتخاب تصادفی نبود. یک هلیکوپتر معمولی برای چنین مأموریتی بیش از حد بزرگ و سنگین بود. Little Bird برای عملیات ویژه ساخته شده است: کوچک، چابک، کمحجم و مناسب برای فرود و پرواز در مناطقی که یک هلیکوپتر بزرگتر عملاً نمیتواند وارد آنها شود. راز احتمالاً در «Little Bird» نیست؛ در Little Birdِ مخصوص است اینجاست که پاسخ معمای کین شکل میگیرد. آنچه امروز تقریباً میتوان با اطمینان گفت این است که خانواده هلیکوپتر مورد استفاده، «Little Bird» بوده است. حتی CBS در روایت خود از عملیات، صراحتاً از «small Little Bird helicopters» نام برده است. گزارشهای تخصصی نیز مشخصتر شدهاند و از MH-6 Little Bird بهعنوان محتملترین مدل یاد کردهاند. هلیکوپتر MH-6 Little Bird اما «MH-6» بهتنهایی احتمالاً تمام داستان نیست. Little Birdها در ارتش آمریکا توسط یگان ویژه هوانوردی ارتش، یعنی هنگ ۱۶۰ عملیات ویژه ــ مشهور به Night Stalkers ــ به کار گرفته میشوند و خانوادهای از پیکربندیهای مختلف را شامل میشوند. MH-6 اساساً برای جابهجایی نیرو طراحی شده، در حالی که AH-6 نسخه مسلح این خانواده است. بنابراین صرف گفتن «Little Bird» مشخص نمیکند دقیقاً کدام پیکربندی، چه تجهیزات و چه تغییراتی در آن به کار رفته است. شواهد موجود حتی نشان میدهد که چهار فروند از این هلیکوپترهای کوچک پس از عملیات در ایران باقی ماندند و برای جلوگیری از افتادن تجهیزات حساس به دست طرف مقابل، منهدم شدند. این موضوع اهمیت فناوری بهکاررفته در آنها را بیشتر میکند. بنابراین محتملترین پاسخ این است: هلیکوپتر مورد استفاده برای نجات براوو به احتمال بسیار زیاد یک MH-6 Little Bird از یگان 160th SOAR بوده، اما مدل دقیق، پیکربندی و تجهیزات آن همچنان محرمانه است. و دقیقاً همینجا سخنان کین معنا پیدا میکند. اگر صرفاً «Little Bird» موضوع محرمانه بود، انتشار آن در گزارشهای رسمی و رسانهای آمریکایی منطقی نبود. آنچه واشنگتن احتمالاً میخواهد پنهان کند، نه نام عمومی هلیکوپتر، بلکه نسخه دقیق، تغییرات اعمالشده، تجهیزات شناسایی و ارتباطی، سامانههای کاهش امضا یا شیوه عملیاتی آن در یک مأموریت عمیق در خاک طرف مقابل است. این احتمال وقتی جدیتر میشود که بدانیم آمریکاییها حتی دو MC-130J را که در خاک نرم گیر کرده بودند، منهدم کردند تا فناوری حساس آنها به دست ایران نیفتد. در چنین عملیاتی، «سختافزار» تنها یک وسیله حملونقل نیست؛ هر قطعه میتواند بخشی از تواناییهای اطلاعاتی و عملیاتی آمریکا را آشکار کند. بنابراین هلیکوپتر تارشده در «60 Minutes» احتمالاً یک راز کاملاً ناشناخته نیست. راز واقعی، چیزی است که داخل آن هلیکوپتر قرار داشته است. آنچه تصویر محوشده کین به ما میگوید این نیست که آمریکا نمیخواهد کسی بداند «Little Bird» در ایران بوده؛ این موضوع عملاً دیگر فاش شده است. پیام اصلی این است که آمریکا هنوز نمیخواهد کسی بفهمد دقیقاً کدام Little Bird، با چه تغییراتی و با چه تواناییهایی، توانسته در یکی از حساسترین عملیاتها در درون خاک ایران حضور پیدا کند. و شاید به همین دلیل است که در مستندی که قرار بود داستان نجات یک خلبان را روایت کند، مهمترین هلیکوپتر داستان هنوز پشت یک لکه تار باقی مانده است. تبلیغات نویسنده : مصطفی جرفی چرا آمریکا تصاویر هلیکوپتر نجات در ایران را تار کرد؟ خبرگزاری فرانسه: بازرگانان ایرانی حضور مستحکمی در بازارهای قدیم دبی دارند آمادهباش اسرائیل با تسلط نیروهای یمنی بر سواحل جنوبی دریای سرخ و تنگه بابالمندب زیدآبادی: همه در برابر قانون برابرند، اما ظاهراً برخی برابرترند! بیشتر بدانید: جنگ ایران و آمریکا جنگنده https://www.fararu.com/fa/news/1001992/%.body: دانشآموز خردسال تبریزی، در رقابتهای جهانی المپیاد انفورماتیک نوجوانان IJIO ۲۰۲۶ درخشید و با عملکردی موفق، مدال طلای این مسابقات را به دست آورد. سالار رضا محمدی، دانشآموز پایه اول ابتدایی در رقابت با شرکتکنندگانی از کشورهای مختلف جهان، در بخش مربوط به پایه تحصیلی خود به مقام نخست رسید تا یک افتخار بینالمللی دیگر برای ایران رقم بخورد. سالار رضا محمدی پیش از این نیز در حوزههای مختلف علمی و مهارتی استعداد خود را نشان داده است. جهش تحصیلی از پایه اول به چهارم ابتدایی، کسب مقام در مسابقات شطرنج تیمی، مهارت در حل مکعب روبیک، تسلط به زبان انگلیسی و گذراندن دورههای رباتیک بخشی از سوابق اوست. این نخبه خردسال تبریزی همچنین در نمایشگاههای بینالمللی نقاشی حضور داشته و مجموعهای از توانمندیهای علمی، هنری و مهارتی را در کارنامه خود ثبت کرده است. پ ، پـ تبلیغات تبلیغات تبلیغات لحظهای از زندگی کفتارهای در پارک ملی گلستان هدیه اردوغان به عروس خانم کودک ۷ ساله تبریزی شگفتیساز شد سوختن درخت پس از سقوط روی سیمهای برق بیشتر بدانید: کودک تبریز نخبه المیرا شریفی مقدم تبلیغات عکس؛ تقدیر از المیرا شریفی مقدم تکذیب ماجرای ربوده شدن ۵۰ کودک تبریزی هفت گرم طلا انگیزه قتل کودک ۶ ساله

https://www.fararu.com/fa/news/1002002/%.body: مدیرعامل باشگاه فجرسپاسی شیراز توضیحاتی درباره سربازی علیرضا بیرانوند و امکان حضور او در تیم شیرازی مطرح کرد. پ ، پـ تبلیغات تبلیغات حاتم احمدی مدیرعامل باشگاه فجرسپاسی درباره بحث سربازی علیرضا بیرانوند و تأکید سردار رادان فرمانده انتظامی کل کشور بر اعزام به خدمت او در مهرماه اظهار داشت: چیزی که من شنیدم این است که علیرضا بیرانوند امروز دفترچه اعزام به سربازی خود را پُست میکند. حالا باید ببینیم زمان اعزام او اول مهر اعلام میشود یا اول آبان. قبل از فصل پیگیر بودیم ولی الان بیرانوند برای ما کارایی ندارد و تا نیمفصل نمیتواند بازی کند. در صورت آمدن به تیم ما هم باید تا نیمفصل فقط کنار تیم تمرین کند. وی افزود: قبلاً که پیگیر وضعیت بیرانوند بودم اعلام کردم این بازیکن از اول مهرماه سرباز است و دیگر ارفاقی به او نمیشود، اما نمیدانم برخی چرا به او گفتند که در تراکتور بماند و سربازیاش را عقب میاندازند. فجرسپاسی یک باشگاه صد درصد نظامی است و هر تصمیمی که ستاد کل بگیرد برای ما قابل احترام است. بیرانوند هم یک بازیکن ملی است و برای او احترام قائل هستیم. «آیا برای حضور بیرانوند در فجرسپاسی مذاکرهای با او یا ستاد کل نیروهای مسلح داشتهاید؟» مدیرعامل باشگاه فجر در پاسخ به این سوال گفت: کسانی که سرباز میشوند اختیارشان دست ستاد کل نیروهای مسلح است. صحبتهایی با ستاد انجام دادم. اولویت هم ما هستیم. چند روز پیش از ستاد کل نیروهای مسلح هم با من تماس گرفتند و گفتند که بیرانوند از اول مهرماه سرباز است و هیچ ارفاقی دیگری به او نخواهد شد. حاتم احمدی در پاسخ به این پرسش که آیا امکان دارد بیرانوند یک نیمفصل در تیم نیروی زمینی در لیگ دسته اول بازی کند و بعد به فجر سپاسی بپیوندد، گفت: خیر چنین امکانی نیست. اگر سربازی «کد» یک ارگان نظامی را بگیرد دیگر امکان تغییر آن وجود ندارد. قانون چنین اجازهای نمیدهد. تبلیغات منبع : تسنیم والیبال ایران چطور سهمیه المپیک ۲۰۲۸ میگیرد؟ بیرانوند محل خدمت سربازیاش را مشخص کرد؟ در یک مورد خاص، طارمی بهتر از دایی است! تراکتور - شباب الاهلی؛ بدون بیرانوند و با چند معمای مهم بیشتر بدانید: علیرضا بیرانوند فجر سپاسی تبلیغات تراکتور - شباب الاهلی؛ بدون بیرانوند و با چند معمای مهم تصویر؛ اولین واکنش بیرانوند بعد از خبر اعزام به سربازی با دستور اکید سردار رادان؛ بیرانوند اول مهر سرباز میشود

https://www.uscirf.gov/religious-prisone.body: Defending Freedoms Project | USCIRF Skip to main content Search Sort by Relevance Order Asc Desc Search Defending Freedoms Project The Defending Freedoms Project In December 2012, the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission in the U.S. House of Representatives, in conjunction with the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) and Amnesty International USA , launched the Defending Freedoms Project (DFP) to support prisoners of conscience around the world. The DFP aims to increase attention to human rights abuses by encouraging Members of Congress to advocate on behalf of prisoners of conscience wherever they may be found. The Project allows Members to stand in solidarity with the prisoner, let them know they have not been forgotten, and encourage accountability for unjust treatment. In recent years, the DFP coalition has expanded to include Reporters without Borders (RSF), Freedom House , Freedom Now , Scholars At Risk , PEN America , and the Senate Human Rights Caucus. USCIRF nominates individuals to the Project who are imprisoned specifically for exercising their right to freedom of religion or belief and pairs them with a Member of Congress to advocate on their behalf. Any Member of Congress who chooses to support the case of a prisoner is provided with a detailed toolkit to help facilitate his/her advocacy efforts. By taking on a prisoner’s case, the Member could contribute to the release or reduction of a prison sentence or the improvement of prison conditions, while also raising awareness about the unjust laws or policies that led to imprisonment. Learn more about the Defending Freedoms Project .

https://www.uscirf.gov/news-room/release.body: Malaysia Plans to Return 5,000 Rohingya to their Persecutors | USCIRF Skip to main content Search Sort by Relevance Order Asc Desc Search Malaysia Plans to Return 5,000 Rohingya to their Persecutors Aug 14, 2026 Malaysia Plans to Return 5,000 Rohingya to their Persecutors Washington, DC – Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim recently indicated his government’s decision to repatriate approximately 5,000 Rohingya refugees to Burma after Burma’s ruling military junta, the Tatmadaw, had agreed to accept them. Later the Prime Minister noted they could not return Rohingya if they would be persecuted or their lives threatened. Although repatriation is considered a positive step for refugees if it is safe to return, the Prime Minister should know that sending civilians into an active war zone puts them at grave risk. This is particularly true for those belonging to groups that the receiving government has targeted with war crimes and acts of genocide, such as predominantly Muslim Rohingya. “ Violence and human rights abuses in Burma continue to escalate for minority religions and civilians, and forcing Rohingya survivors to return would put their lives at extraordinary risk by exposing them to armed conflict, forced conscription, and an ongoing humanitarian crisis ,” said Vice Chair CeCe Heil . “ The Tatmadaw’s sustained airstrikes and persistent violations of international humanitarian laws continue to result in extensive civilian casualties and the large‐scale displacement of vulnerable religious minorities .” Malaysia’s announcement came at a time when Rohingya residing in Malaysia are facing escalating challenges. A surge in online threats recently forced at least nine schools serving Rohingya children to close, while police detained more than 100 Rohingya asylum seekers who had gathered at the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) office in Kuala Lumpur after hostile residents in Penang state drove them out of their temporary homes. Although around 126,000 Rohingya are registered with the UNHCR in Malaysia, that country does not formally recognize Rohingya as refugees and it is neither a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention nor its 1967 Protocol. “ The U.S. government has supported the needs of Rohingya fleeing persecution through the World Food Program; now is the time for the State Department to re-double the message directly with Malaysia that its help for these desperate families is both vital and appreciated ,” said Commissioner Gunisha Kaur . “ Pushing Rohingya into the hands of their persecutors would contribute to perpetuating ten years of atrocities that have impacted many of Burma’s vulnerable religious groups .” In its 2026 Annual Report , USCIRF recommended that the U.S. Department of State continue to designate Burma as a “Country of Particular Concern,” or CPC, for engaging in systematic, egregious, and ongoing violations of religious freedom. USCIRF also recommended Malaysia’s inclusion on the State Department’s Special Watch List for engaging in or tolerating severe violations of religious freedom. ### The U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) is an independent, bipartisan federal government entity established by the U.S. Congress to monitor, analyze and report on religious freedom abroad. USCIRF makes foreign policy recommendations to the President, the Secretary of State and Congress intended to deter religious persecution and promote freedom of religion or belief. To interview a Commissioner, please contact USCIRF at [email protected] .

https://www.uscirf.gov/news-room/op-eds/.body: The Hill: The cost of India’s anti-conversion laws | USCIRF Skip to main content Search Sort by Relevance Order Asc Desc Search The Hill: The cost of India’s anti-conversion laws Dec 19, 2025 The op-ed was originally published by The Hill on December 19, 2025. By U.S. Representative Glenn Grothman, USCIRF Chair Vicky Hartzler and Vice Chair Asif Mahmood The two most populous countries in the world have very troubling issues related to freedom of religion or belief. China’s atrocious record dictating people’s beliefs and practices is well known, but the largest democracy in the world, India, has a less well-known record — and it’s getting worse. Twelve of India’s 28 states currently enforce anti-conversion laws, intended to restrict religious conversion through certain means, such as deceit or coercion. In practice, authorities use this law to unjustly arrest hundreds of religious leaders for allegedly conducting “forced” conversions to Christianity or Islam, in some cases stoking communal tensions and mob violence. Recently, the state of Goa, known not only for its beautiful beaches, but also for its religious sites — including the Churches and Convents of Goa, a UNESCO World Heritage Site — announced its intent to follow suit with its own anti-conversion law. Home to over 1.4 million people, it is also home to a sizable Christian community, who make up around 25 percent of its population. Goa’s Chief Minister said that his state needs such laws to prevent “noticed cases of ‘love jihad,” a Hindu Nationalist conspiracy theory that men are entrapping Hindu women in marriages to convert them to Islam. But the new law in Goa likely will not just impact Muslims. Indeed, in Uttar Pradesh State, an official in India’s ruling Hindu Nationalist party filed a complaint based on anti-conversion laws against pastor Jose Pappachan and his wife, Sheerja, alleging that they had attempted to “forcibly convert” Hindu neighbors to Christianity through their programs to provide food and education. Although the lack of evidence led to their initial release on bail, a stricter law was passed in early 2024, and the couple was convicted and sentenced to five years in prison in January 2025. The passage and enforcement of these laws across India — in combination with a range of other policies designed to repress religious minority communities across the country — undermine religious freedom and harm innocent citizens. For example, the State of Madhya Pradesh has changed its law to require a minimum six-month imprisonment before bail is even granted, with potential fines increasing ten-fold to $12,000, which is harsher than the treatment murder defendants receive. State officials of Madhya Pradesh have even gone so far as to suggest the death penalty be the punishment for alleged forced conversion. We strongly urge Secretary of State Marco Rubio to designate India as a Country of Particular Concern under the International Religious Freedom Act. Not only will the designation comply with the law, it will reinforce the importance and need that freedom of religion or belief for all is a universal right and shared value. As a country looking to strengthen its relationship with the U.S., the repeal of anti-conversion laws is a way India can demonstrate its commitment to this timeless and shared value. Glenn Grothman, a Republican, represents the 6th District of Wisconsin in Congress, Vicky Hartzler is chair of the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom, and Asif Mahmood is vice chair of the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom.

https://24.kg/english/388881_Call_censor.body: Call censorship, detention without ID: What proposed in Kyrgyzstan for wartime - | 24.KG English 15:45, 11 September 2026 , Bishkek - 24.kg news agency , by Turdubek AIGYROV Call censorship, detention without ID: What proposed in Kyrgyzstan for wartime 15:45, 11 September 2026 , Bishkek - 24.kg news agency , by Turdubek AIGYROV A draft constitutional law has been submitted for public discussion in Kyrgyzstan that significantly alters the procedures authorities must follow during states of emergency and martial law. One of the key proposals is to expand the grounds for declaring a state of emergency. The list is set to include acts of terrorism, as well as armed border incidents and conflicts that threaten the lives and safety of residents in border areas. If police and civil protection forces are insufficient to contain a crisis, units and formations of the Armed Forces—as well as other military formations—may be deployed. The proposal seeks to designate the Security Council as the supreme body for operational command and force coordination during a state of emergency. Additionally, territorial coordination headquarters could be established in one or more regions. The draft also revises curfew regulations. It specifies that curfews would be imposed for a set period, prohibiting citizens from being outside their homes or traveling between settlements without a pass and ID. Under martial law, military patrols would be authorized to detain violators until the curfew ends. Individuals lacking IDs could be detained until their identity is established, for a maximum of two days. Provisions are also included for personal searches, inspections of belongings and vehicles, and the confiscation of weapons, ammunition, and other prohibited items. During martial law, the president would have the authority to establish a special regime for airspace usage, including temporary flight bans. Proposed measures also include military censorship of mail, telecommunications, media publications, and telephone conversations, including those directed abroad. Procedures for responding to a sudden attack are outlined separately. Military command bodies and other military formations would be required to repel aggression without waiting for a formal declaration of war or the official imposition of martial law. The amendments also clarify the powers of the Cabinet of Ministers, the procedure for establishing territorial defense committees, and the interaction between state bodies. https://asiaplus.news/en/2026/09/11/the-.body: Central Asia Communication Economics First block train from China to Iran launched via Central Asia A train of 55 containers is set to cover more than 6,000 kilometers in approximately two weeks. asia+ 11.09.2026 14:05 Telegram Facebook WhatsApp Copy URL The first block train carrying cargo from China to Iran via Central Asia has been launched, with 55 containers traveling through Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan, Interfax Kazakhstan reports, citing the press service of Uzbekistan Railways’ container operator Uztemirjulcontainer. The containers carry automotive components, consumer goods and other consolidated cargo. The train will travel through China, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan before entering Iran via the Sarakhs railway crossing. Kazakhstan is the first transit link after China The train entered Kazakhstan from China through the Khorgos–Altynkol border crossing, according to inbusiness.kz . It departed Altynkol station on September 7 and is continuing toward Uzbekistan. It will leave Kazakhstan through the Saryagash–Keles border crossing before being handed over to the Uzbek side. From Uzbekistan, the train will enter Turkmenistan through the Khojadavlet–Farap crossing and continue toward Sarakhs on the Iranian border. The Khorgos–Altynkol–Keles–Khojadavlet–Farap–Sarakhs–Tehran route is already used by carriers transporting goods between China and Iran. More than 6,000 kilometers in 14–16 days The total route is more than 6,000 kilometers , with delivery expected to take approximately 14–16 days , according to Uztemirjulcontainer. Rail freight therefore offers a middle ground between more expensive air transport and slower sea shipping. Existing rail services between China and Iran via Central Asia typically take around 14–18 days. Uzbekistan offers incentives for transit The China–Iran railway corridor through Central Asia is not entirely new. Cargo has previously been transported through Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan, including routes that bypass Uzbekistan. The new development is the launch of a dedicated block train running through Uzbek territory. Uzbekistan is also offering economic incentives to increase transit traffic. From February through the end of 2026, a 0.60 reduction coefficient applies to tariffs for certain international shipments on the Keles–Khojadavlet section, which is used by trains traveling from Kazakhstan through Uzbekistan to Turkmenistan, according to the Russian customs and logistics portal tks.ru . Regular service could follow Uztemirjulcontainer considers the inaugural train a practical test of the China–Central Asia–Iran transport corridor. If the service meets the expected delivery times and proves reliable, regular block trains could be launched, the operator said. For Kazakhstan, the service could increase container transit from the Chinese border through Altynkol toward Central Asia. Uzbekistan could increase traffic on the Keles–Khojadavlet section, while China and Iran would gain another fully overland freight option that does not depend on sea transportation. https://www.gazeta.uz/en/2026/08/31/uzbe.body: Photo: Press service of the president of Uzbekistan Uzbekistan and India agree to elevate relations to comprehensive strategic partnership. President of Uzbekistan and prime minister of India agreed to elevate the countries' relations to the level of comprehensive strategic partnership. They also discussed increasing trade turnover fivefold by 2030. Shavkat Mirziyoyev awarded Narendra Modi the highest state award for foreign citizens. На русском языке 31 August 2026, 09:38 Politics Uzbekistan and India reached an agreement to elevate their relations to the level of comprehensive strategic partnership. This was announced during talks between president Shavkat Mirziyoyev and prime minister Narendra Modi in Tashkent on Sunday, the presidential press service said . The countries announced the establishment of strategic partnership in 2011. The sides agreed to intensify political contacts and exchanges at all levels, including through the Intergovernmental Commission, the Business Council, and parliamentary friendship groups. The creation of a coordination mechanism at the level of foreign ministers is also planned. Last year, trade turnover exceeded $1 billion for the first time. The sides said there is a potential for a significant increase of this figure — to $5 billion by 2030. Advertising on Gazeta Promising areas of cooperation include energy, electrical engineering, metallurgy, critical minerals, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, agriculture, jewelry industry, and others. In recent years, the number of joint ventures has increased sevenfold. There are 14 direct flights per week between the countries. Uzbekistan and India actively cooperate in education. Four Indian universities operate in Uzbekistan. The Lal Bahadur Shastri Centre for Indian Culture and the Mahatma Gandhi Centre for Indology play a key role in developing cultural and humanitarian ties. Yoga is also growing in popularity in Uzbekistan. During his visit, Narendra Modi met with the leadership of the Yoga Federation. The development of interregional cooperation was particularly noted. Partnerships have been established between Andijan region and the state of Gujarat, Fergana region and the state of Haryana, and Samarkand region and Agra. The leaders emphasized the need to continue the practice of mutual support for initiatives within the UN, SCO, BRICS, and other international organizations. Highest Degree Friendship Order Following the talks, president of Uzbekistan presented the Indian prime minister with the Order of Dostlik (Friendship) of the Highest Degree. This is Uzbekistan’s highest state award for foreign citizens. “For his enormous personal contribution to strengthening the historical friendship and wide-ranging strategic partnership between the Republic of Uzbekistan and the Republic of India, special services in deepening and elevating multifaceted cooperation to a new level, developing political, trade, economic and investment ties, and intensifying cultural and humanitarian exchanges between the peoples of the two countries,” the presidential decree states. “I am confident that, thanks to our shared aspirations and efforts, our multifaceted and long-term relations will continue to develop dynamically,” president of Uzbekistan noted. This order has previously been awarded to Chinese president Xi Jinping, Russian president Vladimir Putin, UN secretary-general António Guterres, chairman of the Halk Maslakhaty of Turkmenistan Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov, president of Kazakhstan Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and president of Turkmenistan Serdar Berdimuhamedov. Signed documents During the Indian prime minister’s visit, the following documents were signed : Memorandum of Understanding on Economic and Financial Dialogue; Programme of cultural exchanges between governments for 2026−2030; Agreement on cooperation in the field of higher education and scientific research; Agreement on cooperation in the field of environmental protection; Tourism Cooperation Program for 2026−2028; Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in the Field of Geology and Mineral Resources; Memorandum of Understanding on cooperation in the field of Ayurveda and other types of traditional medicine; Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation in the Field of Archival Affairs; Memorandum of Understanding on Cooperation between the University of World Economy and Diplomacy and the Sushma Swaraj Institute of Foreign Relations; Agreement on the establishment of partnership relations between the Samarkand region and the state of Gujarat. https://24.kg/english/389057_Kyrgyzstans.body: Kyrgyzstan’s debt to China stands at $1.4 billion - | 24.KG English 11:18, 14 September 2026 , Bishkek - 24.kg news agency , by Aizada KUTUEVA Kyrgyzstan’s debt to China stands at $1.4 billion 11:18, 14 September 2026 , Bishkek - 24.kg news agency , by Aizada KUTUEVA Kyrgyzstan’s debt to China stands at $1.4 billion, Deputy Finance Minister Umutzhan Amanbaev said at a meeting of the Zhogorku Kenesh Committee on Agrarian Policy, Water Resources, Subsoil Use, Ecology and Environmental Protection. The committee was discussing a report on the execution of the republican budget for 2025. Amanbaev was responding to MP Ismanali Zhoroev, who asked why Kyrgyzstan’s debt, according to an infographic, has been growing since 2017. According to Amanbaev, China’s share of Kyrgyzstan’s debt previously accounted for up to 40 percent of the total. «Later, it fell to 27 percent. I would like to note that until 2020, this debt amounted to as much as 90–100 percent of the country’s total budget revenues. We have now analyzed the figures for the first seven months of this year and would like to note that the debt to China accounts for only 16 percent of the country’s budget revenues. In other words, we could repay the entire debt today without any problems, but it is better, of course, to adhere to the repayment schedule and gradually reduce the debt, which is what Kyrgyzstan is doing,» he said. The deputy minister added that all loans are now being taken solely for development purposes and are linked to economic growth. «Some 77 billion soms have been allocated for debt servicing, 70 percent of which is for external debt. We currently have no overdue payments. https://www.trend.az/azerbaijan/4223542..body: Home Azerbaijan Azerbaijani and Chinese SSS' sign security cooperation agreement (PHOTO) Azerbaijan Press release 14 September 2026 11:56 (UTC +04:00) Photo: State Security Service of the Republic of Azerbaijan Alish Abdulla Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 14. Azerbaijan and China have signed an agreement on cooperation in ensuring security, covering areas including counterterrorism, combating transnational organized crime and fraud involving telecommunications systems. The agreement was signed between the State Security Service of the Republic of Azerbaijan and the Ministry of Public Security of the People’s Republic of China at the end of a meeting between Chairman of Azerbaijan’s State Security Service (SSS), Colonel-General Ali Naghiyev, and Chinese Minister of Public Security Wang Xiaohong, a member of the State Council of the People’s Republic of China. The Azerbaijani delegation led by Naghiyev visited Lianyungang in China’s Jiangsu Province at the invitation of the Chinese Ministry of Public Security. As part of the visit, the delegation participated in the fifth Global Public Security Cooperation Forum, which brought together senior officials representing various countries and international organizations. The forum discussed counterterrorism, strengthening international partnerships, the use of new technologies in this area and improving governance mechanisms. The event adopted a final document titled the "2026 Action Plan on Global Counterterrorism." At the meeting with Wang Xiaohong, the sides exchanged views on the current global security situation and the nature of modern threats, highly assessed the current level of relations between the two institutions and considered prospects for future cooperation in areas of mutual interest. The sides stressed the importance of joint efforts to address growing threats based on mutual trust and respect, as well as operational information exchange, amid a more complex international environment, ongoing military conflicts in some regions and additional risks to the global economy. They noted the strategic nature of relations between Azerbaijan and China, based on the principles of respect for sovereignty and mutual support. The sides expressed their intention to contribute to the implementation of agreements reached between the two countries’ heads of state, deepen cooperation in combating terrorism, transnational organized crime and fraud committed through telecommunications systems, and further develop ties between law enforcement and security agencies. Naghiyev thanked the Chinese side for the invitation and expressed his condolences to the Chinese people and the families of those killed in the disaster in Tibet, which also claimed the lives of citizens of other countries. He stressed that the Azerbaijani people shared China’s grief over the losses and stood in solidarity with those affected. On a year-on-year basis, Chinese investment flows changed from a net outflow of $21.6 million in the second quarter of 2025 to a net inflow in the same period of 2026. The difference between the two periods amounted to approximately $241.1 million, according to Trend calculations. Trend 's calculations also reveal that China's net investment in Georgia amounted to $8.2 million for full-year 2024 and included a net outflow of $44.3 million in 2025. The second quarter of 2026 therefore represented the highest quarterly level of Chinese investment recorded in Geostat's available data series starting from 2024. China accounted for 46.8% of Georgia's total FDI inflows in the second quarter, ahead of the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates. The figures highlight changes in the geographic composition of foreign investment flows during the period. https://www.azernews.az/analysis/263747..body: France moves into Armenia as Russia’s influence fades 13 September 2026 15:49 (UTC+04:00) Ulviyya Poladova Read more Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan concluded his visit to France, which was the first one since his party’s victory in the June parliamentary elections and the worsening of relations with Russia over the unresolved question of Yerevan’s choice between the EU and the EAEU. His meeting with President Emmanuel Macron, who paid a state visit to Armenia in May and took part in the 8th summit of the European Political Community, demonstrated the strengthening alliance between Yerevan and Paris and Armenia’s pro-European course. The talks in Paris showed that the French leader remains Armenia’s main lobbyist within the European Union. The formal reason for Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s latest visit to Paris was an invitation to attend the International Space Summit, held in the French capital on September 9-10. But the real story goes much deeper than space. The worse relations between Russia and Armenia become, the more Armenia’s attention turns toward Europe. France remains one of the EU countries supporting Armenia’s integration into the union, as Yerevan seeks to reduce its dependence on the Russian market, logistics and energy system. It is also interesting that literally on the eve of Pashinyan’s trip to Paris, France changed its ambassador in Yerevan. On September 5, Florian Escudier took up his post, replacing Olivier Decottignies, during whose tenure French-Armenian military cooperation became particularly active. The choice of his successor was also quite telling. Escudier had previously worked, among other things, on strategic security and cybersecurity issues. The new ambassador himself quickly explained what he intended to focus on in Yerevan. On September 7, he said he wanted to bring relations between the two countries to an "unprecedented level," specifically naming economic diplomacy and defense cooperation among his priorities. So, after the declarations made in May, Paris appears ready to move toward more practical cooperation. One of the first such projects is expected to be the Bargushat Tunnel. It will become part of the Sisian-Kajaran section of the North-South corridor and will significantly improve connections between central Armenia, Syunik and, further south, Iran. Yerevan hopes this will allow it to maintain a reliable route to the south and reduce its dependence on future transport links through Azerbaijan. The strengthening of relations with France, with which Armenia has historically maintained close ties, takes on particular importance in the context of the Armenian government’s broader pro-European course. Much of this process is focused on political steps and ambitious plans for the distant future, such as visa liberalization. Europe’s economic contribution, particularly that of France, remains modest, although during the first half of 2026, trade between Armenia and the EU almost doubled and exceeded $516 million. At the same time, French involvement in the TRIPP (Zangezur Corridor) project cannot be ruled out. In the future, Armenia could, in exchange for certain services, as French support for joining the EU and provide access to this project, which is already being developed with U.S. involvement. The TRIPP project itself envisages the creation of a joint venture in which the United States would receive rights to develop and manage the transport corridor for 49 years. This is taking place against the backdrop of growing tensions between the United States and France in recent times. This raises the question of whether Armenia can sit on several chairs at the same time. On the one hand, there is the United States, which will be involved in the Zangezur Corridor, and France, which is both an ally and Armenia’s potential gateway to the European Union. On the other hand, there is Iran, which is at war with the United States, and Russia, which remains under EU sanctions, including those imposed by Paris. And will Moscow be pleased to see a NATO country operating right next door, even if only as a contractor or project partner? In the defense sector, France has helped Armenia diversify its sources of military equipment after Armenia moved away from the CSTO and Russia. Paris has signed agreements on the supply of French equipment and the training of Armenian military personnel. Purchases have included armored vehicles, night-vision equipment, Thales radars and Caesar artillery systems. Back in May, France and Armenia agreed to expand cooperation in military technologies and defense systems. Now space is being added to this cooperation. Modern space technologies have long been about much more than satellites for scientific purposes. They include communications, navigation, surveillance, intelligence and a wide range of dual-use technologies. France is willing to open this door for Armenia as well. It is in Paris’s interest to tie Yerevan more closely to its own and European technological projects, complementing the growing French presence in Armenian defense and infrastructure with cooperation in advanced technologies. Nikol Pashinyan is not simply a passive beneficiary of France’s growing interest in Armenia. The relationship between Yerevan and Paris is increasingly based on a convergence of interests, in which both sides see strategic value in a deeper partnership. The more actively France becomes involved in Armenia’s defense, infrastructure, economy and technology, the more alternatives to Russia Yerevan gains. However, this partnership is not without limits. Armenia’s attempt to diversify away from Russia inevitably intersects with the interests of other regional and global powers. France therefore has to balance its growing engagement with Armenia against its wider relationships and commitments. Specialists from Uzbekistan’s Uzbekhydroenergo are studying China’s experience in using artificial intelligence, digital technologies and cybersecurity systems in hydropower as part of a technical research and knowledge-sharing program. This was reflected in the statement by the Uzbekhydroenergo. A delegation from O‘zbekgidroenergo is examining advanced approaches to the digitalization of hydropower facilities, the introduction of artificial intelligence and information security technologies, and the development of smart hydropower plants during a visit to China. As part of the practical program, the Uzbek delegation visited the Inlyanbao Hydropower Plant on the Dadu River in Sichuan province. Specialists are reviewing the plant’s digital control and automation systems, intelligent monitoring technologies and information security solutions used in day-to-day operations. The visit also includes an exchange of practical experience on the effective operation and protection of digital systems deployed at hydropower facilities. The Inlyanbao plant has a total installed capacity of 1,116 megawatts, comprising four main 270-MW hydropower units and an additional 36-MW unit. Maintenance work is currently being carried out on the 36-MW generator. The facility includes an approximately 15-kilometer diversion tunnel for directing water, while the powerhouse is located underground. As one of the major energy facilities in the cascade of hydropower plants along the Dadu River, Inlyanbao provides an opportunity for Uzbek specialists to examine how digital and intelligent technologies can be integrated into modern hydropower operations. “The experience gained in China will help accelerate digital transformation, expand the use of artificial intelligence and strengthen information security in Uzbekistan’s hydropower sector,” O‘zbekgidroenergo said. The knowledge-sharing program is expected to support further modernization of Uzbekistan’s hydropower industry and help specialists assess technologies that could be applied to improve the management, monitoring and security of hydropower facilities. The visit reflects Uzbekistan’s efforts to expand the use of digital solutions and artificial intelligence across the energy sector while strengthening technical cooperation and knowledge exchange with China. https://english.news.cn/20260914/1098396.body: World's first museum devoted to prehistoric flying reptiles opens in NW China's Xinjiang-Xinhua World's first museum devoted to prehistoric flying reptiles opens in NW China's Xinjiang Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-09-14 09:43:15 Visitors view pterosaurs replicas at a science museum in Hami, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, Sept. 13, 2026. (Photo by Polat Niyaz/Xinhua) URUMQI, Sept. 14 (Xinhua) -- A science museum focused on pterosaurs, a winged reptile closely related to dinosaurs, opened on Sunday in Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region in northwest China. The world's first of its kind, this museum is located in a national geopark in Xinjiang's Hami region, a location renowned for abundant pterosaur fossil discoveries. With an exhibition area of about 4,600 square meters, the Hami Pterosaur Museum consists of six oval-shaped halls in a staggered layout. Seen from above, it resembles a clutch of pterosaur eggs resting in the desert. This video screenshot shows a science museum focused on pterosaurs in Hami, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, Sept. 12, 2026. (Photo by Zhang Xuhui/Xinhua) Fossils on display include specimens recovered during more than two decades of rescue excavations by researchers from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). Also on display are the world's first 3D preserved fossilized pterosaur eggs and embryos, along with large pterosaur specimens making their public debut. This is the first time all of these specimens have been displayed together. The exhibits present a panoramic recreation of pterosaur life and evolution during the Cretaceous period roughly 130 million years ago, the museum said. Xu Xing, head of the CAS institute, said the museum not only highlights China's leading role in global pterosaur research but also offers the public a window to experience scientific discovery up close and appreciate the wonders of ancient life. ■ You may like Two teachers devote their lives to a remote mountain village Chinese dance drama "A Dream of Red Mansions" makes U.S. debut in New York A glimpse of Yinxu Museum in Anyang, China's Henan EcoChina | A scenic drive into Hainan's rainforest InPics | Shougang Park reinvents itself as vibrant urban destination Pinglu Canal to become operational on Sept. 16 More from GLOBALink BRICS cooperation: Shared prosperity for half of world's population What BRICS family saw at CIFIT: markets, investment and new partnerships How AI is reshaping everyday services at CIFTIS Follow us on More from GLOBALink BRICS cooperation: Shared prosperity for half of world's population What BRICS family saw at CIFIT: markets, investment and new partnerships How AI is reshaping everyday services at CIFTIS Follow us on World's first museum devoted to prehistoric flying reptiles opens in NW China's Xinjiang

https://www.specialeurasia.com/2026/08/1.body: Iran-Tajikistan and the Persian-Speaking Union Proposal Persian-Speaking Union Proposal: Iran-Tajikistan Bilateral Outlook Image generated using artificial intelligence technology Executive Intelligence Snapshot Iran and Tajikistan are actively expanding a bilateral partnership based on common Persian heritage, broadening their focus from foundational cultural exchange toward joint technical, energy, and economic initiatives. Despite ongoing conflict in the Persian Gulf, the Proposal of a “union of Persian-speaking countries and regions” illustrates that Tehran remains committed to a pragmatic, non-ideological Central Asian policy aimed at building regional cooperation. Simultaneously, Central Asian states continue to view Iran as an indispensable security partner and a vital gateway for maritime trade and transport infrastructure. Background On 16 August 2026 , during a meeting with Tajik Minister of Energy and Water Resources Dalir Jum’a , Iranian First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref proposed establishing a “Union of Persian-Speaking Countries and Regions” to strengthen cultural and civilisational cooperation among Persian-speaking communities. The Iranian diplomat stressed that that Iran and Tajikistan’s shared cultural, civilisational and linguistic heritage provides a strong foundation for expanding bilateral relations. Relations between Tehran and Dushanbe experienced a deep freeze from 2015 to 2019, triggered largely by Iran hosting Muhiddin Kabiri, the leader of the Islamic Renaissance Party of Tajikistan (IRPT) at a conference. In response, Tajikistan restricted the activities of various Iranian organizations within its borders. Tensions escalated further in 2017 when Tajik state television aired a documentary accusing Iran of subversion during Tajikistan’s 1990s civil war. Iranian authorities have consistently denied these allegations. To this day, contemporary sources remain divided on whether Tehran funded insurgent groups, as conclusive evidence has never emerged. Since 2021, a total strategic reset occurred , yielding visa-free travel , defence cooperation (the opening of an Ababil-2 drone factories in Tajikistan), and dozens of Memorandums of Understanding signed across trade, energy, infrastructure, cultural exchange, and security sectors. Bilateral trade turnover grew substantially over recent years, jumping from $377.7 million in 2024 to approximately $483.9 million in 2025, a roughly 28% year-on-year increase. Continued upward trajectory persisted into 2026, with first-half trade reaching $254.3 million (up 14.8% compared to the same period in 2025). In 2025, Iran entered the top five of Tajikistan’s largest trading partners, ranking fifth by total trade turnover. Iran’s primary exports include petrochemical products (oil bitumen, polyethylene, polypropylene), construction materials (cement, clinker), and agricultural/food products (sugar, pasta, citrus fruits). High-level bilateral commission meetings between officials (such as Tajikistan’s Ministry of Energy and Water Resources and Iran’s Oil Ministry) have established ongoing supply agreements for diesel, crude oil, and aviation fuel. Furthermore, to sustain trade momentum, both nations have advanced transport initiatives, including planned direct railway connectivity via Turkmenistan to optimise cargo and supply chain movements across Central Asia. Why Does It Matter? The proposal by Iranian First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref to establish a union of Persian-speaking countries and regions is a pan-Persianist soft-power posturing , which has long characterised the two countries ties. Relations with Central Asia underwent a complete step-change under the Raisi presidency. It is no coincidence that these shifts materialised after 2021, the year of his election. Acting in alignment with the directives set out by Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei, Raisi vigorously pursued Iran’s “Look East” policy following years of inconclusive diplomacy aimed at rekindling ties with European markets. Although relations with individual Central Asian republics had experienced friction in preceding years, the thirteenth Iranian administration reversed the trend, ushering in an unprecedented wave of state visits. The success of these policies stems from mutual necessity: for Tehran, the northern frontier serves as an economic relief valve away from the south-western borders, where Iran finds itself militarily encircled. Conversely, for landlocked republics, Iran offers vital access to international waters and direct connectivity to Gulf and Indian markets. Now Tehran wants to lock in this momentum. Facing sustained Western isolation, Iran leverages Pan-Persian cultural rhetoric as a low-cost vehicle to anchor itself in Eurasia. It frames trade, transit infrastructure, and scientific transfers under a shared civilizational umbrella. The Organization of Turkic States (OTS) , driven by Turkey, Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan, and Kazakhstan, has gained massive momentum in Central Asia. Iran feels culturally and geopolitically squeezed by Turkic block-building . Promoting a Persian-speaking alliance serves as Tehran’s counterweight to Ankara’s expanding influence in the region. This strategy has gained even more urgency as the US war on the Islamic Republic is favouring the Western-led Middle Corridor, which regional actors currently view as safer. While with “union of Persian-speaking countries” Aref clearly referred to Tajikistan, with “regions” he implicitly references the non-Pashtun, Dari-speaking populations of Afghanistan (Tajiks, Hazaras). Since the Taliban takeover, both Tehran and Dushanbe share deep security anxieties regarding Sunni extremism , ethnic Pashtun dominance, and cross-border terrorism, even as both navigate complex, pragmatic realities with Kabul. Iran has been a major player in countering regional Sunni terrorism and has a relevant role in the security architecture established by the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) . Being Tajikistan one of Central Asian most affected countries, the security issue might lay a common ground for cooperation. President Emomali Rahmon will not sign up for an anti-Western or anti-Russian bloc. Tajikistan depends on Moscow for security, Beijing for financial support, and Western/Gulf investments for development and humanitarian aids. Dushanbe will take Iranian energy, transit (Chabahar port), and trade, but will reject risky institutional alignment that might trigger secondary sanctions. Iran, in fact, is an Islamic Republic with Shia-centric power structures. Tajikistan is a hyper-secular state that aggressively suppresses political Islam . Rahmon would view religious influence from Tehran as a threat to his regime’s survival. Nevertheless, unlike in the Middle East where the deterrence posture of Iran also required spreading religious influence to build the so-called Axis of Resistance, Tehran’s approach to Central Asia has been characterised by a pragmatic strategy with bilateral relations based on trade, security and common infrastructure. While Aref rightly pointed to cultural and civilisational cooperation , this also marks a revival. Decades of Soviet engineering severed direct cultural ties between the populations. For instance, Tajiks use the Cyrillic alphabet, while Iranians use the Perso-Arabic script. Moreover, while Afghanistan officially recognised the name “Dari” for its dialect of Persian in its 1964 Constitution to promote a national identity distinct from Iran, the Soviet Union did artificially codify “Tajik” as a separate language in the 1920s to weaken regional Persian cultural continuity following 19 th century imperial conflicts between the Russian and Qajar empires over shared borderlands. This broader Soviet strategy of national delimitation also led to the inclusion of historic Persian cultural centres like Samarkand and Bukhara within Uzbekistan rather than Tajikistan. https://kun.uz/en/news/2026/09/14/six-de.body: Image: https://tviibb.uz/oz/news/foizsiz-kredit-bu-tuzo The regional Department of Internal Affairs said authorities opened a criminal case under Article 168 (Fraud), detained six suspects, and continued the investigation. The department said the suspects posted online advertisements offering interest-free loans and invited interested citizens to pre-rented luxury offices. They allegedly offered to arrange loans in the citizens’ names and then took a portion of the funds disbursed by banks. The suspects allegedly promised citizens that they could arrange UZS 100 million loans in their names, give them UZS 50 million and keep the remaining UZS 50 million for the company, while covering the monthly repayments themselves. They assured the citizens that they would not face any problems, the department said. Citizens trusted the promises and applied for the loans using their phones. More than 400 citizens ended up with loans in their names, while the suspects allegedly took half of the funds disbursed. The total amount involved was nearly UZS 17 billion, the department said. After some time, banks began sending citizens demands to repay the loan debt. During pre-investigation checks and operational activities, police detained six members of the group as suspects and placed them in custody. The investigation continues.

https://www.gazeta.uz/en/2024/12/19/susp.body: Photo: sledcom.ru Citizen of Uzbekistan detained in Moscow on suspicion of killing Russian general Russia’s Investigative Committee announced the arrest of a citizen of Uzbekistan for a terrorist attack in Moscow that killed general Igor Kirillov and his assistant. Authorities claim the suspect confessed during interrogation to being “recruited by Ukrainian intelligence services”. На русском языке Ўзбек тилида O‘zbek tilida 19 December 2024, 12:09 World The Investigative Committee of Russia (ICR) announced the arrest of a suspect in connection with a terrorist attack in Moscow that killed the head of the Russian Armed Forces' Radiation, Chemical and Biological Defense Troops Igor Kirillov and his assistant Ilya Polikarpov. According to the ICR, the suspect, born in 1995, is a citizen of Uzbekistan whose name has not been disclosed. However, Telegram channel Baza identified him as Ahmad Kurbanov. During interrogation, the suspect allegedly admitted to being “recruited by Ukrainian intelligence services”, the ICR stated. Advertising on Gazeta “Following their instructions, he arrived in Moscow and obtained a homemade explosive device. He placed it on an electric scooter parked near the entrance of the residential building where Igor Kirillov lived. To monitor the serviceman’s residence, he rented a car-sharing vehicle equipped with a surveillance camera. Footage from this camera was streamed live to the organizers of the attack in Dnipro. Once the servicemen were seen exiting the building, the explosive device was remotely detonated,” the Investigative Committee said. A video of the suspect’s interrogation has also surfaced on social media. The ICR alleges the suspect was promised $100,000 and relocation to a European country in exchange for carrying out the attack. The Russian Interior Ministry said the suspect was apprehended in the village of Chornoye, near the city of Balashikha in Moscow region. The embassy of Uzbekistan in Moscow said it had established contact with the Russian law-enforcement bodies and was clarifying the information about the detained. General Igor Kirillov and Ilya Polikarpov were killed in the explosion on 17 December while leaving their residence on Ryazansky Prospekt in Moscow. Investigators say the explosive device was concealed in the electric scooter near the building’s entrance. The ICR opened criminal cases on charges of murder, terrorism and the illegal circulation of explosives. Reuters and The New York Times , citing sources in Ukrainian intelligence, reported that the assassination of Kirillov was orchestrated by Security Service of Ukraine (SSU). A day before his death, the SSU accused Kirillov in absentia of being responsible for the mass use of chemical weapons against Ukrainian forces. https://kaktus.media/doc/552944_aktivist.body: kaktus.media Активисты проведут фотовыставку "Неоткрыточный Кыргызстан". Принять участие может каждый Общество 1274 9 сентября 2026 10:29 Kaktus Все самое интересное в Telegram Жителей Кыргызстана приглашают принять участие в фотовыставке и показать другую сторону своих городов, которую не увидишь на открытках, – повседневную, противоречивую и настоящую. Такой анонс распространили активисты урбанистической инициативы Peshcom. Больше новостей и видео в Telegram-канале Kaktus.media. "Горы, озера, ущелья, национальные орнаменты и архитектурные достопримечательности – именно таким Кыргызстан чаще всего предстает на фотографиях. Но страна, в которой мы живем, выглядит совсем иначе, если смотреть на нее не глазами туриста, а глазами человека, который каждый день идет по одной и той же улице, сидит во дворе, едет в маршрутке, покупает курут на тротуаре или ищет место, где можно просто побыть, - говорится в объявлении. - Нам важно увидеть, как выглядят наши города, когда не фотографируют достопримечательности и открыточные виды. Нам важно дать возможность самим жителям рассказать о своих городах – таких, какими они их знают, чувствуют и проживают". О чем жители Кыргызстана могут рассказать на выставке? Авторы могут предложить фотоработы на одну из пяти тем: "Кому принадлежит город?" Кто имеет право на городское пространство и кто решает, как им пользоваться? Пешеходы или автомобили? Парк или торговый центр? Можно ли продавать курут на тротуаре? Для кого в городе трава, если на ней нельзя сидеть? Авторы могут представить работы, которые исследуют доступ к городскому пространству, осмысляют право на город и наше место в нем. "Нетуристические места в городе". Истории дворов, домов, тротуаров, городских огородов, барахолок, о "третьих местах", местных жителях и других местах и сюжетах, которые редко попадают в путеводители, но составляют повседневную жизнь города. "Современные вызовы". О том, с какими изменениями и проблемами сталкиваются города Кыргызстана сегодня: климатическими изменениями, качеством воздуха, городской мобильностью, доступом к воде, исторической памятью, новой архитектурой и другими актуальными вопросами. "Guilty pleasure – постыдное удовольствие". О том, что приносит радость, но одновременно вызывает легкий стыд или смущение. Маленькие удовольствия от города, которые мы почему-то считаем нелогичными или "не по правилам". Сидеть там, где нельзя. Идти не по маршруту. Необъяснимый комфорт в секретном месте. Бесплатное удовольствие.. А может быть, это не guilty pleasure, а город не оставляет выбора? "Свободная тема". Авторы могут предложить собственный взгляд на город или право на него. Кто может участвовать? По словам организаторов, принять участие в выставке может любой желающий. "Неважно, снимает ли автор десять лет или фотографирует на камеру телефона совсем недолго. Не нужны художественное образование, профессиональная техника или выставочный опыт. Организаторам важнее другое – собственный взгляд на город и история, которую автор хочет рассказать. К участию приглашают не только фотографов и художников, но и обычных жителей разных городов и регионов Кыргызстана", - сказано в анонсе. Принимаются фотографии, фоторепортажи, видео, инсталляции, перформансы, фотозины. Можно подать как одну работу, так и серию. Работы должны быть на кыргызском, русском и английском языках. https://www.gazeta.uz/en/2023/11/28/russ.body: Photo: Sergey Lantyukhov / news.ru Russia’s MIA suggests imposing new restrictions on illegal migrants Russia’s Ministry of Internal Affairs proposed to introduce a controlled stay regime for illegal migrants, along with a number of bans and restrictions. Those appearing in the register will not be able to drive, transfer money or get married. 28 November 2023, 17:37 World Russia’s Ministry of Internal Affairs (MIA) proposed to introduce a controlled stay regime for illegal migrants, which provides for a number of prohibitions and restrictions for them. TASS reported this news with reference to MIA’s draft law. “Controlled stay is a legal regime applied [...] to a foreign citizen staying in the Russian Federation and has no legal grounds for stay (residence) in the Russian Federation or who has knowingly provided false information or documents in the course of migrants' registration,” the agency quotes an excerpt from the document. According to the document, a foreign citizen is considered to be in the regime of a controlled stay from the date of entering personal information in the register. The grounds for this may be: expiration of the term of temporary stay, temporary residence permit, residence permit; illegal border crossing; annulment of visa, refugee status or temporary asylum, citizenship. Those under control are obliged to inform about their whereabouts, change of place of stay, date, place and route of planned independent departure from Russia. In case of violation, they can be deported. Advertising on Gazeta At the same time, foreigners will have the right to request the reasons justifying applicability of the controlled stay regime to them. They will also be able to appeal against the actions or omissions of officials. The bill sets consequential limitations on those to whom such a regime applies. These are: a ban on state registration of legal entities and individual entrepreneurs; a ban on the purchase and sale of real estate, vehicles and self-propelled machines; a ban on placing real estate on the country’s cadastral registration; a ban on state registration of vehicles; a ban on driving a car, a possible denial in taking licensure examinations and replacement of driving licenses. In addition, Russia’s MIA proposes to restrict illegal migrants from opening bank accounts, transferring money and marrying . According to MIA, innovations will help to identify illegal migrants and “remove” them from the territory of Russia. Now in Russia there are 6.4 million foreign citizens. Most of them arrived to the country for working purposes, the head of the main department of MIA on migration Valentina Kazakova has reported earlier. In 2022, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan were listed as the three leaders in terms of the inflow of migrant workers to Russia. На русском языке Ўзбек тилида O‘zbek tilida 9 August 2026, 09:04 Sport The 19-year-old Uzbekistan defender Behruz Karimov signed a contract with Swiss club Lugano, the Uzbekistan Football Association said . Karimov, born on 7 August 2007, began his football career at the Odil Junior academy before joining Tashkent-based Olympic. In February 2025, he moved to Termez-based Surkhon. The right-back quickly established himself in the Uzbekistan league and earned a call-up to the national team. At the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Karimov started in Uzbekistan’s matches against Colombia and Portugal. Karimov is also considered one of Asia’s most promising young footballers. According to the CIES Football Observatory, which assessed the performances of players under 19 over the past season against their peers in the same position, Karimov ranked second among Asian players. Founded in 1908, Lugano is one of Switzerland’s oldest football clubs. The team has won the Swiss Super League three times and the Swiss Cup four times. Advertising on Gazeta Lugano finished third in the 2025/26 Swiss Super League, recording 19 wins, 10 draws and nine defeats in 38 matches to collect 67 points. The result earned Lugano a place in the UEFA Conference League qualifying rounds. Earlier, another Uzbekistan national team defender, 22-year-old Jakhongir Urozov, joined Russian club Rubin Kazan. His former club Dinamo Samarkand said he had joined the Kazan side on loan until the end of 2026, with an option to buy. Urozov’s contract with Dinamo runs until the end of 2027. Urozov joined Dinamo in 2024 and made 55 official appearances over three seasons, scoring one goal. His performances for the club earned him a call-up to the Uzbekistan national team. At the 2026 FIFA World Cup, he featured in matches against Colombia and DR Congo. https://www.gazeta.uz/en/2024/04/16/free.body: Photo: Freedom House Freedom House: Democracy Score in Central Asia continues to decline Democratic performance in Central Europe and Central Asia continues to decline, with the war in Ukraine and other conflicts having hastened geopolitical shifts in the region, Freedom House reports. Uzbekistan’s democracy level is rated at 1.18 out of 7 points. O‘zbek tilida Ўзбек тилида На русском языке 16 April 2024, 20:53 World A persistent decline in democratic performance in Central Europe and Central Asia for the past 20 years was revealed in the annual report “Nations in Transit 2024” by Freedom House, the international human rights organization. The report covers 29 countries in the region. Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the conflict in Nagorno-Karabakh, and other events in recent years “have accelerated a geopolitical reordering in the region, with countries sorting themselves into two opposing blocs: those committed to a liberal, democratic order and those that violently reject it”, the report stated. Over the past year, 10 countries in the region suffered declines in Democracy Score, while just five earned improvements. Experts attribute the region’s “failure” in consolidating democracy to authoritarian and anti-democratic leaders. Freedom House classified Democracy Scores in Azerbaijan, Belarus, Russia and all Central Asian countries as “Consolidated Authoritarian Regimes” . Among the “Hybrid Regime” countries are Armenia, Georgia, Hungary, Moldova, Ukraine and others, totalling 11 states. Advertising on Gazeta The “Semi-Consolidated Democracies” category encompassed 10 countries, including Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, and Poland. Freedom House notes that all eight countries in the “Consolidated Authoritarian Regimes” category continued to “lead the race to the bottom” over the past year. Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, which “previously scored one the less repressive end of the authoritarian range, now fit the broader Central Asian trend of authoritarian consolidation,” according to the organization. Uzbekistan received a Democracy Score of 1.18 out of a possible 7 points in Freedom House’s assessment. Last year’s score was at 1.21 points. Kyrgyzstan’s Democracy Scores decreased to 1.64 points (from 1.68), while Kazakhstan’s dropped to 1.29 (from 1.32). Tajikistan and Turkmenistan received Scores of 1.04 points and 1 point respectively. Belarus scored 1.11, while Russia and Azerbaijan scored 1.07 points each. Among the highest scorers in the region, Estonia led with a score of 6, followed by Latvia and Slovenia, each with a score of 5.79. Ukraine’s democratic development was rated at 3.43, followed by Armenia at 3.07 and Georgia at 3.04. In March, Freedom House published its annual freedom rating, with Uzbekistan scoring 12 out of a possible 100 points. All Central Asian countries were classified as “not free”. https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/eng/zy/jj/dstzg.body: Chinese Ambassador to Myanmar Ma Jia Publishes a Signed Article Titled “Fostering Unity Through the Rule of Law and Advancing Shared Prosperity Through Development” in Myanmar’s Official Media_Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China IPC Visas English EN 简体中文 Français Español Русский عربي HOME THE MINISTRY Main Responsibilities The Minister Principal Officials Departments Related Agencies NEWS Top Stories Speeches Diplomatic Schedule New Ambassadors MFA News Spokesperson’s Remarks News from Overseas Missions RESOURCES Communiqués Foreign Policies In Focus Diplomatic History Diplomatic Figures Protocol Affairs Map of China OVERSEAS MISSIONS Chinese Embassies Chinese Consulates General Chinese Missions to International Organizations and Representative Offices Abroad COUNTRIES AND REGIONS Asia Africa Europe North America South America Oceania ABOUT CHINA Home Resources In Focus Chinese Chiefs of Mission On the Governance of China From Ambassadors Chinese Ambassador to Myanmar Ma Jia Publishes a Signed Article Titled “Fostering Unity Through the Rule of Law and Advancing Shared Prosperity Through Development” in Myanmar’s Official Media Updated: August 07, 2026 12:23 (From Chinese Embassy in Myanmar) On August 5th, Ambassador Ma Jia published a signed article titled “Fostering Unity Through the Rule of Law and Advancing Shared Prosperity Through Development” in Myanmar’s official media, including Global New Light of Myanmar and Myanma Alinn Daily. The full text is as follows: On July 1 this year, the Ethnic Unity and Progress Promotion Law of the People’s Republic of China came into force. The law marks three historic firsts. For the first time, it incorporates General Secretary Xi Jinping’s important thought on strengthening and improving work on ethnic affairs into national legislation. For the first time, it clarifies in legal terms such as fostering a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation and advancing the building of a community for the Chinese nation. For the first time, it defines in law the framework for work on ethnic affairs in the new era. It is a successful example of translating the major theoretical achievements and practical experience in work on ethnic affairs into the will of the state through legislation, providing a solid legal foundation for promoting ethnic unity and progress in the new era. I would like to take this opportunity to introduce to our friends from all sectors in Myanmar the law’s guiding principles, institutional framework, and practical results, and to share China’s experience and thinking on promoting ethnic unity and progress through the rule of law. First, the law establishes the fundamental principles for work on ethnic affairs by upholding equality among all ethnic groups and fostering a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation. From the outset, it makes equality among all ethnic groups the basic principle governing work on ethnic affairs and explicitly prohibits all forms of ethnic discrimination and oppression. It provides legal guarantees for the equal participation of all ethnic groups in state governance and for sharing the benefits of development. It upholds the combination of national unity and regional ethnic autonomy, as well as the combination of ethnic factors and regional factors, while safeguarding the equal rights of ethnic minorities in political, economic, cultural, and other fields. Regardless of population size, every ethnic group is an equal member of the Chinese nation, united by a shared future. Guided by the goal of fostering a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation, the law fully respects cultural diversity. It protects by law the freedom of all ethnic groups to use and develop their own spoken and written languages, and the freedom to preserve or reform their customs and traditions. It uses the rule of law to uphold harmony among diverse cultures while enabling every ethnic culture to flourish in its own way. Second, the law promotes integration and shared development by creating more opportunities for interaction and integration among all ethnic groups, encouraging people to live, study, work, and enjoy life together. Promoting extensive interaction and integration among ethnic groups is a central task set out in a dedicated chapter of the law. Today, two-way population mobility has become the norm in China. More than 33 million ethnic minority people live and work away from their registered hometowns, and over one-third of the ethnic minority population now resides in urban and dispersed areas. The pattern of “overall integration, local concentration, mutual interaction” continues to deepen. The law sets out detailed measures covering education, culture and tourism, sports, employment, and community development. It includes specific provisions for building integrated communities and promoting interaction and integration through education, cultural activities, sports, and tourism. These measures help people of different ethnic groups deepen mutual understanding, strengthen mutual respect, bridge differences, build consensus, and make the concept of the Chinese national community part of everyday life. Third, the law focuses on improving people’s well-being through balanced development so that all ethnic groups can share the benefits of Chinese modernization. It is designed to promote common prosperity and development for all ethnic groups. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the combined GDP of China’s five ethnic autonomous regions has grown from RMB 3.25 trillion to RMB 8.66 trillion in recent years, more than doubling in size, while regional development gaps have continued to narrow. From the northern frontier to the south, and from the plateau to the border regions, ethnic minority areas have made major advances in transport, energy, communications, and other fields. Public services in education, healthcare, housing, and social security have continued to improve. Behind these steady gains are real improvements in people’s sense of fulfillment and well-being. The best way to assess a country’s ethnic policy and governance is to look at the facts, examine its development, and see whether people’s lives have truly improved. In China’s ethnic minority areas, high-speed railways have reached border regions, highways now extend to remote villages, and power grids cover even mountainous areas. Schools have been built close to where people live, hospitals are equipped with advanced facilities, and housing conditions have improved greatly. Traditional cultures are also thriving. Ancient epics continue to be passed down, traditional festivals are celebrated with renewed vitality, and intangible cultural heritage is being preserved from generation to generation. In Xinjiang, GDP reached RMB 2.14 trillion in 2025, more than doubling compared with 2012. Xinjiang produces over 90 percent of China’s cotton and has more than 22 million mu of vineyards, jujube orchards, and other specialty fruit plantations. Installed new energy capacity has exceeded 100 million kilowatts, providing strong momentum for economic transformation. The region has more than 8,000 schools of all types, with over six million students enrolled, while access to education continues to improve. Primary healthcare services now cover the entire region. At the same time, the Uyghur Muqam art form and the “Manas” epic have been inscribed on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The lawful use of ethnic languages is fully protected, and traditional music, dance, and handicrafts are being systematically preserved. In Xizang, GDP exceeded RMB 300 billion in 2025, nearly tripling compared with 2012. Major infrastructure projects, including the Qinghai-Xizang Railway, the Lhasa-Xigaze Railway, and the Ya’an-Xigaze section of the Sichuan-Xizang Railway, continue to advance. https://thediplomat.com/2026/09/another-.body: Credit: Facebook / Saida Mirziyoyeva Subscribe for ads-free reading Saida Mirziyoyeva has another new job. By presidential decree – that is, by order of her own father, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, whose administration she heads – Mirziyoyeva has been appointed manager of the Tashkent International Financial Center (TIFC). The TIFC was proposed in a March 2026 presidential decree as part of an effort to bring in long-term foreign direct investment. The financial center aims to attract investors in a range of industries from banking, investment, and insurance services to digital assets, Islamic finance, and green tech, in addition to professional services like auditing, legal counsel, and fintech. Signed into law in July , the TIFC will operate under a special legal regime, based on English law, with a unique regulatory framework and an independent commercial court. With this arrangement, Uzbekistan seeks to address long-standing concerns foreign investors have had by carving out a legal space that isn’t governed strictly by Uzbek law. In pursuit of attracting foreign investors, those engaged in the TIFC will reportedly be able to hire foreigners without obtaining the usually required work permits and take advantage of special entry visa options. They will be allowed use foreign currency or cryptocurrency for payments and other monetary obligations and will benefit from tax and customs breaks until 2076. In announcing the signing of the law in July by Mirziyoyev, Mirziyoyeva said on social media, “This is one of the most important pieces of economic news of the year and the result of reforms that we pursued for almost ten years.” She went on to argue that the TIFC’s special structures “are the mechanisms to which global investors, banks, investment funds and international financial companies are accustomed. This new regulatory ecosystem should make the country more attractive for capital, modern financial services and major international projects.” According to a Telegram statement posted by presidential press secretary Sherzod Asadov, as manager, Mirziyoyeva will organize the agenda and preside over meetings in the absence of the financial center’s chairman – the chairman is, by law, Mirziyoyev. She will coordinate the TIFC’s launch and represent the financial center in dealings with international organizations, investors and partners – both those abroad and in Uzbekistan. She will have the authority to conclude agreements, establish working groups and “engage experts.” In June 2025 , Mirziyoyeva was appointed head of the presidential administration, effectively becoming her father’s chief of staff. Uzbekistan’s government does not have a vice president post, making Mirziyoyeva the highest-ranking official after her father. In August 2026 , Uzbekistan adopted a new law regulating the presidential administration that granted Mirziyoyeva sweeping new powers – everything from judicial reforms to anti-corruption, and an automatic seat on the Security Council – and lifetime immunity to boot. She holds an extraordinarily wide range of power while being subject to no accountability outside of her father’s opinion. Now she’s also in charge of Tashkent’s ambitious gambit to attract foreign investment. Uzbekistan is not unique in turning to family to consolidate power. In neighboring Tajikistan, President Emomali Rahmon’s son, Rustam Emomali, holds a variety of important positions – he’s chairman of the National Assembly and also mayor of the capital, both posts he was appointed to by his father, in 2020 and 2017 , respectively. As chairman of the Nation Assembly, Emomali is constitutionally next in line for the presidency, should his father resign or otherwise vacate the post. In Turkmenistan, Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov passed the presidency on to his son Serdar in 2022 before government changed its structure to give the elder Berdimuhamedov a new position technically above that of the president .
